The last iterate then converges to a single Nash equilibrium in every two-player zero-sum matrix game, even with multiple equilibria. Near a unique equilibrium, the set of active actions freezes after one round, and the linearized dynamics have a closed form. Take the payoff matrix restricted to these active actions and centered by the game value. Whenever the limiting step size times this matrix's largest singular value is less than one, the last iterate converges linearly at a closed-form rate. Across $216$ random games, all $184$ instances with a numerically resolved limit satisfy this condition. The predicted rate matches the empirical rate with a median ratio of $1.000$. Our analysis also shows that the per-round increase in the squared regret norm scales with the squared Nash gap, which measures distance to equilibrium. In sequential games (extensive-form games), exact gap computation requires a costly best-response pass. On Kuhn and Leduc poker, the analogous norm increase tracks the Nash gap between infrequent passes. Our code is available at https://github.com/lbn187/NormCert

papers.title: From Reconnaissance to Response: Quantitative Risk Parameterization and Game Theoretic Containment in Modern Enterprise Attack
papers.abstract: Modern Security Operations Centers struggle with delayed manual incident response, enabling adversaries to advance through the Cyber Kill Chain during early stage reconnaissance. While classical game theoretic defense models optimize strategic resource allocation, they rely on static utility matrices that fail to adapt to dynamic telemetry. This paper presents an integrated, metrics driven decision engine that bridges quantitative risk parameterization and continuous automated response time. Common Vulnerability Scoring Systems exploitability parameters are mapped to attacker success probabilities and evaluate defender log distributions via Factor Analysis of Information Risk Monte Carlo simulations. Real time SIEM logs streams are modeled as Poisson process arrival rates, dynamically updating defender posterior threat belief through sequential Bayesian filtering. A closed form threshold is derived by framing the interaction as a dynamic Bayesian Stackelberg game, where the expected unmitigated risk exceeds proactive containment cost. Parameterized against empirical data from the 2023 MGM Resorts and Caesars Entertainment cyber incident, simulation results demonstrate that the engine suppresses transient background noise while triggering automated SOAR network isolation within seconds of adversarial probing. Multi parameter sensitivity analysis confirms that the decision boundary dynamically adjusts to live perimeter vulnerability, offering a control theoretic foundation for sub minute automated threat containment.

papers.title: Sparse-View Interpretable 3D Animal Behavior Representations for Neural Encoding and Decoding
papers.abstract: A deeper understanding of brain function requires a precise, structured characterization of behavior. Yet, extracting behavioral representations from video in a form suitable for scientific analysis remains a fundamental challenge. Many prior studies represent behavior via pose estimation or nonlinear video embeddings. However, pose tracking discards rich information beyond predefined keypoints, while nonlinear video embeddings lack interpretability. We address this limitation with SABLE (Sparse-view Animal Behavior Latent Embeddings), a self-supervised framework that leverages a geometric inductive bias to learn behavior representations. By augmenting a multi-view transformer with priors from monocular depth and pose estimation, SABLE reconstructs 3D animal behavior from extremely sparse views while learning explicit 3D latent structure. Without ground-truth 3D labels, it reliably recovers 3D behavior from two-view videos, whereas state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods fail or yield degenerate solutions. Across the International Brain Lab and Cheese3D datasets, we demonstrate that SABLE learns 3D representations that match or exceed prior SOTA performance in neural encoding and decoding. Single-neuron analyses further identify neurons with putative 3D tuning, generating testable hypotheses about how the brain represents 3D behavior. Once pretrained across animals, SABLE serves as an off-the-shelf model that generalizes zero-shot to unseen animals without animal-specific calibration or retraining. Our method establishes 3D-aware video embeddings that capture complex behavior, opening new avenues for studying brain-behavior relationships.

papers.title: DirectUV: Image-Conditioned UV Texture Generation with Surface-Aware Positional Encoding
papers.abstract: Generating high-quality UV textures for 3D meshes remains challenging. Multi-view projection pipelines suffer from occlusion and view inconsistency, and recent methods that generate textures directly in UV space still rely on auxiliary modules to supply 3D information, leaving the attention mechanism tied to UV-grid positions rather than to the underlying surface geometry. This mismatch limits coherence across seams and disconnected UV islands. We propose DirectUV, an image-conditioned UV texture diffusion framework that operates in the latent UV space of a pretrained image VAE, in which a Diffusion Transformer denoises the UV latent given a single input image and a coarse UV map. At its core, Surface-Aware Positional Encoding (SAPE) replaces the standard 2D-grid positional encoding with encodings derived from per-token 3D surface coordinates obtained via UV-to-surface correspondence. As positional encodings define the distance metric used by attention, SAPE enables tokens to interact according to 3D positional proximity derived from surface correspondence rather than UV-grid distance, restoring coherence across seams and disconnected islands. A multi-level extension further assigns different attention heads to progressively finer subdivisions of the same latent UV patch, allowing the model to reason about surface structure at multiple granularities. Experiments show that DirectUV produces sharper and more globally consistent textures than other baselines, with the largest improvements in occluded and view-unseen regions where projection-based methods leave gaps or stretched textures.

papers.title: Forensic Twins: Self-Supervised Residual Learning for AI-Generated Image Forensics
papers.abstract: Detectors of AI-generated images are typically trained using samples from specific Generative AI architectures and degrade as soon as a new architecture emerges. Recent approaches have explored self-supervised pre-training as an alternative solution, yet standard frameworks work against the forensic task, since their augmentations overwrite the micro-statistics of image formation. This paper introduces Forensic Twins, a Self-Supervised Residual Learning (SSRL) framework whose pretext task removes shared image content between views. Each image is mapped through a forensic residual extractor, from which two spatially disjoint crops are drawn. Sharing no pixel, the two views leave the redundancy-reduction objective with a predominantly content-independent common signal, the stationary fingerprint of the image acquisition pipeline. The encoder is exclusively trained on real images; no AI-generated image is used to learn the representation. Experiments show competitive results in zero-shot, few-shot, and linear probing scenarios, reaching 97.21% AUC across 26 unseen AI generators, including GANs, diffusion models, and commercial systems. We also provide insightful analysis on the learned representation regarding unsupervised clustering on different AI generators and its forensic properties. Code, weights and exact splits are publicly available.

papers.title: The word problem in verbal products of groups
papers.abstract: We prove that nilpotent and metabelian products of groups with decidable word problem have decidable word problem. In contrast, we exhibit families of groups with decidable word problem for which their solvable product has undecidable word problem. In doing so, we exhibit hyperbolic groups with undecidable membership problem in their derived subgroups.

papers.title: A framework for linking literature-based knowledge integration and infrastructure-supported knowledge integration: Opportunities and challenges from a case study
papers.abstract: Integrating knowledge across disciplines is central to sustainability research, yet most evidence-synthesis methods rely on findings as reported in publications, limiting verification and reuse of underlying data and workflows. We develop a conceptual framework linking literature-based and infrastructure-supported knowledge integration, using a systematic review case study to examine when integration can extend beyond reported findings. We reviewed 37 studies on climate change, violent conflict, and household food security. Literature-based synthesis enabled integration across all included studies, whereas access to reusable outputs was limited: over half provided no data availability statement, 27% reported availability upon request, but reusable data and workflows were available for only 8%. To explore infrastructure-supported integration, we used the TIB Knowledge Loom to represent studies with accessible data and code as machine-readable outputs, and produced a knowledge gap map (KGM) from manually extracted and Loom-derived data, comparing manual and infrastructure-supported synthesis. Where outputs were reusable, synthesis could be produced directly from data and workflows rather than from publications. These findings show that literature-based synthesis can be complemented by infrastructure-supported integration where outputs are accessible and usable, and that advancing knowledge integration depends not only on infrastructures but on making data, code, and workflows accessible, executable, and reusable.

papers.title: Bins
papers.abstract: I characterize the undominated ways of transmitting, storing, and organizing information under capacity constraints, showing that they take a precise geometric form. Under a regularity assumption on the information to be organized, they are convex subdivisions of the space of beliefs constructed by recursively subdividing cells according to weighted proximity criteria.

papers.title: Hilbert functions over the exterior algebra and f-vectors in higher rank I: Amata-Crupi monomial modules, Kozlov polytopes, and r-vectors of simplicial complexes
papers.abstract: Let $E$ be the exterior algebra on $n$ generators over a field, and let $F$ be a graded free $E$-module with $r$ generators, of degrees $d_1 \le \dots \le d_r$. We determine the convex hull of the set of Hilbert functions of the quotients $F/M$, where $M$ runs over the monomial submodules of Amata and Crupi. The hull is the Minkowski sum of $r$ shifted copies of one and the same simplex: the Kozlov simplex, which Kozlov proved in 1997 to be the convex hull of the $f$-vectors of simplicial complexes on $n$ vertices. For $r=1$ the statement is Kozlov's theorem, so this is a rank-$r$ generalization of it. We give a self-contained proof, including a proof of Kozlov's theorem from the local Lubell-Yamamoto-Meshalkin inequality, which is in essence Kozlov's own second proof, and the facet description of the Kozlov simplex that this proof contains. Along the way we isolate the class of submodules for which the argument works, the ideal-direct-sum modules, and show by example that the Hilbert function of a graded submodule outside that class need not be a shifted sum of $f$-vectors at all. The combinatorial content is stated separately, in language that uses no algebra, as a result on $r$-vectors of simplicial complexes and their $ff$-vectors. Finally we determine the vertices of the Minkowski sum at rank two: which sums of vertices of the summands survive as vertices. The facet descriptions at rank two, conjectured in the first version of this paper, and the vertex and facet descriptions at every rank are proved in Part IV of this series.

papers.title: ClimTip-GML: A global bias-corrected and downscaled dataset for assessing impacts of climate tipping events
papers.abstract: Assessing the impacts of future climate scenarios including tipping events of major Earth system components such as the Amazon rainforest (ARF) or the Atlantic meridional overturning circulation (AMOC), requires accurate and high-resolution simulations. Here, we present ClimTip-GML, the first globally bias-corrected and downscaled climate dataset for impact assessment of large-scale tipping scenarios, comprising eight key variables at 0.25° spatial resolution from three general circulation models (GCMs): CESM1-CAM5, HadGEM3-GC31-MM, and MPI-ESM1-2-HR. The dataset includes 100-year-long climate simulations with preindustrial and historical conditions, as well as scenarios at a +2°C warming level with and without tipping transitions of the AMOC or ARF. We apply generative machine learning (GML) techniques trained on reanalysis data to bias-correct and downscale the GCMs in a manner that is physically consistent across space, time, and all eight variables. Comprehensive validation shows substantially reduced biases, improved small-scale spatial variability, multivariate correlations, and consistent long-term climate responses to the external forcing and tipping events. The results hence permit substantially improved impact assessments of tipping transitions of the ARF and AMOC, directly informing mitigation and adaptation policies.

papers.title: Moving Geometric Objects to Render Their Intersection Graph Connected or Locally Dense
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study graph editing problems on geometric intersection graphs. For a tuple $\mathcal S=(S_1,\dots,S_n)$ of geometric objects in some Euclidean space, let $G_{\mathcal S}$ be their intersection graph. We study the problem of finding a tuple $D=(d_1,\dots,d_n)$ of movement vectors such that the resulting intersection graph $G_{\mathcal{S}+D}$ (after moving, for every $i \in \{1,\dots,n\}$, object $S_i$ by $d_i$) has a predefined property and the total moving distance $\|D\|$ is minimum. In the weighted version, we are also given a weight vector $w=(w_1,\dots,w_n)$ with positive entries, and the objective is to minimise the total weighted moving distance $\|w \cdot D\|$. We first consider the property locally dense, which we define as containment of a $k$-clique. Given $n$ weighted intervals, we solve the problem with respect to this property in $O(k^{1/3} n \log^{1+\varepsilon} n)$ time for any $\varepsilon>0$. We then consider $k$-connectivity for $1\le k \le n-1$. Given $n$ unweighted unit intervals, we solve the problem in $O(n^2 \log n)$ time and, for $k=1$, in $O(n\log n)$ time. For $k=1$, we prove strong NP-hardness on intervals of arbitrary length and on weighted unit disks (with only two distinct weights), and weak NP-hardness on weighted intervals (even when lengths equal weights).

papers.title: Formulation-dependent linearized buckling of stiffened shell panels: role of the stress stiffness operator
papers.abstract: Linearized buckling loads of stiffened panels can diverge across commercial shell formulations because six-degree-of-freedom elements treat drilling rotations and director kinematics differently in the stress stiffness operator. We derive three analytical stress stiffness operators (membrane-only, uncoupled rotational-block, and shear-coupled full second-variation forms), verified against an exact second-difference energy identity. Using direct matrix extraction in ANSYS (SHELL181, SHELL281) and modal and strain-energy benchmarks in Abaqus (S4, S8R), we classify these commercial elements across twelve configurations. On the finest cantilevered shear-panel mesh (in-plane bending and shear), the SHELL181 perturbation and classic procedures predict load factors 11.3% and 28.5% above an independent 3D continuum reference. By contrast, Abaqus S4 and ANSYS SHELL281 lie 5.2% and 5.8% below this reference and remain indistinguishable from the analytical full form within the junction-idealization uncertainty, while Abaqus S8R lies 20.1% below the reference. The tested cases indicate that substantial divergence occurs only when non-coplanar junctions carry pre-stress bending or transverse shear and the buckling mode involves junction drilling rotations. Under pure axial compression or uniform membrane shear flow, the analytical operators coincide and within-element procedures agree within 0.06%. Because buckling under in-plane bending and shear is formulation-dependent, stability design and layout optimization of built-up panels require cross-verification across shell elements or continuum models.

papers.title: Velocity Averaging for the Wigner Equation with Electromagnetic Fields
papers.abstract: We discuss the application of $L^2$-based velocity averaging to the Wigner kinetic equation governing the quantum evolution of the Wigner transform of a density operator of a particle subjected to an external electromagnetic field. This extends the $L^2$-based averaging lemma from [F. Golse, J. Möller: Commun. Math. Sci. (2026)] to electromagnetic fields. We make use of the magnetic or gauge-invariant Wigner transform due to Stratonovich [Sov. Phys. Dokl., 1:414-418, 1956] which differs from the usual definition by a phase factor involving the circulation of the magnetic vector potential along a line segment. The magnetic Wigner transform obeys the Wigner equation in the generalized phase space variables $(x,v=ξ-A(t,x))$, which is a more natural setting for the application of velocity averaging. Since the magnetic Wigner equation contains a first order derivative in the spatial variable, we obtain compactness in $L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ but no gain in regularity.

papers.title: Projective representation theory of spin space groups
papers.abstract: Spin space groups provide the symmetry framework for magnetic crystals with weak spin-orbit coupling, but extracting their physical consequences requires a general theory of irreducible representations. The central difficulty is that spin space groups are represented projectively: their factor systems can render lattice translations noncommuting, induce nonsymmorphic actions in momentum space, and modify the projective structure of little cogroups. These effects lie beyond conventional space-group representation theory. Here, using Mackey's theory of group extensions, we develop a unified constructive framework for all collinear, coplanar, and noncoplanar spin space groups, including antiunitary symmetries and general factor systems. A central result is a canonical decomposition of the relevant factor system $ν$ into a translational factor $σ$, a mixed factor $γ$ coupling translations to point-group operations, and a point-group factor $α$. This decomposition makes transparent how ordinary representation theory is modified: $σ$ determines the projective translation algebra and the appropriate Brillouin zone, $γ$ controls the momentum-space group action and can make it nonsymmorphic, and $α$ contributes to the factor systems of little cogroups. On this basis, we construct all projective irreducible corepresentations by induction over momentum-space orbits. The framework identifies which nonsymmorphic momentum-space symmetries can be realized by spin space groups and how they reconstruct high-symmetry momenta. It reveals Brillouin spaces that are compact flat manifolds, Weyl points of the same chirality locked by projective translation symmetry, and spin space group symmetry-enforced Zak phases as well as Chern insulators. Our results establish the representation-theoretic foundation for systematic studies of weak-spin-orbit-coupled magnetic materials.

papers.title: Exponential Smoothing for Time Series of Random Objects
papers.abstract: Time series of random objects, such as covariance matrices, probability distributions, and functional data, call for forecasting methods that do not rely on arithmetic operations. We introduce geodesic exponential smoothing for time series in Hadamard spaces. The forecast level moves a fixed fraction of the way along the geodesic towards each new observation. The smoothing parameter is estimated by minimising the average squared distance between observations and forecasts. The method involves a single scalar parameter, assumes no stationarity, and updates online in constant time per observation. We further introduce an innovations mechanism under which each observation has conditional Fréchet mean equal to the current level, the metric-space analogue of the innovations state-space model. We show via the quasilinearisation of Hadamard spaces that the level is a martingale in a nonlinear sense, that the spread of the data from the initial state grows at least linearly in time, and that their quasi-autocorrelation at any fixed lag tends to one. We prove almost-sure consistency and asymptotic normality of the smoothing-parameter estimator. Three real-data applications, spanning covariance-matrix, distributional, and functional time series, assess the forecasting performance against structurally heavier alternatives.

papers.title: Counting on Nowhere Dense Classes
papers.abstract: We establish an algorithmic framework for query answering and enumeration in first-order logic with counting on effectively nowhere dense classes of relational structures. Our main technical contribution is an algorithm that, after almost-linear-time preprocessing on a structure $A$ from such a class and a first-order formula $ϕ(\bar{x}, \bar{y})$, can answer the following queries in constant time: given a tuple $\bar{v} \in A^{|\bar{x}|}$, output the number of tuples $\bar{w} \in A^{|\bar{y}|}$ satisfying $A \models ϕ(\bar{v},\bar{w})$. In database terms, this is constant-time evaluation of grouped counting queries. Building on this, we achieve constant-time query answering and constant-delay enumeration for the recently introduced clique-guarded first-order logic with counting (cgFOC) [van Bergerem, Lange, and Schweikardt, MFCS 2026] on effectively nowhere dense classes. These results unify and generalise previous work on nowhere dense classes, namely first-order testing and enumeration [Schweikardt, Segoufin, and Vigny, JACM 2022] and the evaluation of the counting logic FOC1 [Grohe and Schweikardt, PODS 2018]. Moreover, under the assumption $\mathrm{FPT} \neq \mathrm{AW}[*]$, our results are essentially optimal: they do not extend to subgraph-closed graph classes beyond the nowhere dense ones, slight generalisations of the clique-guarding mechanism are intractable even on very simple sparse classes, and very restricted fragments of cgFOC are already intractable on very simple dense classes.

papers.title: ZStar: A unified toolkit for polarization, Born effective charges, dielectric and piezoelectric responses, and infrared and Raman spectra
papers.abstract: Polarization and the response to atomic displacements determine the dielectric, piezoelectric, and vibrational spectroscopy of materials, yet these quantities are usually obtained through separate workflows within ABACUS. Here, we present ZStar, an open-source Python toolkit that unifies these calculations. Using ABACUS and PYATB, ZStar derives Born effective charges (BECs) and zone-center force constants from one symmetry-adapted displacement set, and reuses the displaced electronic matrices for Raman spectra. Berry phases in periodic directions combined with charge-density dipoles in nonperiodic directions extend the method from bulk crystals (3D) to 2D and 1D materials and molecules (0D). These BECs and phonon modes give infrared intensities and the lattice contribution to the dielectric response. From finite strains, ZStar further obtains clamped-ion and relaxed-ion piezoelectric coefficients. This unified workflow reduces the computational cost by up to 4.2$\times$ for BECs and zone-center phonons and 8.4$\times$ for combined infrared and Raman calculations. ZStar also supports machine-learned models by generating training data and post-processing prediction results into physical properties.

papers.title: Population synthesis of low-mass binaries with wind-accreting neutron stars
papers.abstract: We perform population synthesis modeling of neutron star binary systems containing a low-mass main-sequence companion underfilling its Roche lobe. About $10^5$ such systems are expected to exist in the Milky Way. In the majority of such systems, NSs are expected to start accreting the stellar wind matter within a few Gyr, resulting in the appearance of a dim X-ray source. The exact value of this fraction mainly depends on the efficiency of the propeller spin-down, properties of the stellar wind, and common envelope efficiency. Mostly, NSs in such systems are formed in electron capture supernovae. Thus, they obtain a low natal kick. Due to this, the center-of-mass velocities of such binaries are low, too. Only in the case of high common envelope efficiency ($α_\mathrm{CE}\gtrsim 3$), a few tens of long-lived high-velocity binaries can be produced in core-collapse supernovae.

papers.title: EgoPathBench: Evaluating Zero-Shot Egocentric Waypoint Decision-Making in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Widely used spatial-QA benchmarks increasingly motivate embodied navigation, yet evaluate foundation vision-language models (VLMs) through isolated queries about space rather than feasible action sequences in space. However, zero-shot waypoint navigation requires turning spatial understanding into a feasible action sequence: from a single first-person view, a model must jointly ground the target, respect agent-specific clearance, maintain edge-by-edge legality, and stop at the goal. To evaluate this capability, we introduce EgoPathBench, a dataset and five-task benchmark for first-person waypoint decision-making. Each example pairs an egocentric RGB image, a natural-language goal, and numbered visible waypoints, and scores predicted candidate sets or ordered routes against registered 3D scene geometry under task-specific Point or Embodied feasibility graphs. EgoPathBench comprises 31,852 training, 1,345 validation, and 1,111 benchmark questions, with at least one verified reference route for every route question. Across ten foundation VLMs, the highest EgoPath Score is only 35.6. While models often make locally plausible choices and the top model reaches 41.7% success on Point Path, it drops to 10.0% on both Embodied Path and Intent Path, with the remaining nine models below 3% on Embodied Path (and at most 4.0% on Intent Path) -- exposing a sharp gap between local plausibility and complete embodied routes. Beyond evaluation, we construct the EgoPath-SFT training set. Fine-tuning Qwen3.5-4B on EgoPath-SFT raises its EgoPath Score from 3.9 to 38.9, improves closed-loop Isaac Sim execution by 20 percentage points, and transfers consistently to three external spatial benchmarks.

papers.title: Indistinguishability Theory for Identical Particles with Invariant Degrees of Freedom
papers.abstract: Identical particles have dynamically invariant labels in all setups where their degrees of freedom can be partitioned into two parts, which we call internal and visible, with the visible part subject to unitary evolution, while the dynamically invariant internal part accounts for the partial distinguishability of particles. We give the explicit form of the visible state in terms of the indistinguishability function, generalizing the standard symmetrization/antisymmetrization postulate for bosons/fermions with internal modes. The indistinguishability function on the symmetric group accounts for the permutation symmetry of the dynamically invariant label state and gives a self-contained description of the symmetry spectrum of the visible state. It is shown that the indistinguishability of single particles emitted independently from a stable source is completely characterized by the projective measures on the symmetry spectrum. We reveal a hierarchy of successive upper bounds on the projective measure of indistinguishability in terms of marginal projective measures. We point out an experimentally feasible way to get the upper bounds on the indistinguishability of an arbitrarily large number of single photons by direct experimental readout of their marginal projective measures. We also analyze the indistinguishability of coherent superpositions and convex mixtures and resolve a recently posed problem.

papers.title: Scaling Chance-Constrained Correlated Equilibrium Computation for Exclusive Resource-Assignment Games
papers.abstract: The chance-constrained correlated equilibrium concept provides a robust coordination technique for self-interested agents whose costs are uncertain to a central coordinator, but the number of joint actions considered in its computation grows exponentially with the number of agents. We develop a reduced-rank formulation based on convex combinations of chance-constrained pure Nash equilibria to improve scalability. To further reduce computation, we propose an exact-one resource-assignment restriction for games in which agents compete for shared resources and simultaneous use of a resource is undesirable or unsafe. The restriction allows each resource to be assigned to exactly one agent, reducing the number of joint actions considered from O(2^(nr)) to O(n^r) for n agents and r resources. The resulting problem is solved over the restricted joint action set while retaining all incentive constraints associated with unilateral deviations. We show that the feasible set of the restricted problem is exactly the convex hull of the chance-constrained pure Nash equilibria contained in the exact-one assignment set, yielding a necessary and sufficient condition for nonemptiness. We further derive a sufficient condition under which all chance-constrained pure Nash equilibria of the unrestricted game are retained by the restriction. Numerical experiments in a vertiport departure-corridor coordination scenario demonstrate a 99.81% reduction in median computation time relative to the unrestricted formulation while achieving equivalent coordination performance.

papers.title: Principled Detection of Coordinated Manipulation from Aggregate Distortion and Account Reuse
papers.abstract: Coordinated manipulation is collective: plausible accounts can jointly distort ratings, rankings, and engagement. Existing defenses primarily construct evidence from identities, graphs, content, or co-activity. We introduce an aggregate-first evidence layer that treats distortion of a context-level outcome distribution as the primary evidence object. The engine observes only a histogram, count, resolution, and reference distribution; identities are withheld until interval evidence is fixed. Because raw discrepancies have positive finite-sample expectation, we subtract a matched null expectation to obtain signed evidence and account for reference uncertainty. Participation logs then accumulate these fixed increments across accounts. We characterize matched-exposure divergence, bound self-influence, establish finite-horizon separation, and derive an exact linear reuse law for paired contexts. We evaluate the mechanism with controlled rotation experiments and paired counterfactual interventions on historical Amazon review streams. Historical reviews provide the behavioral background; synthetic identities provide known coalition membership, and exact clean twins provide counterfactual controls. In a fixed-attack sweep against historical non-donor comparison accounts, reassigning the same manipulated events across identities with increasing reuse raises account-score ROC-AUC from 0.500 to 0.797. With activity- and exposure-matched clean twins, frequency is at chance while counterfactual attribution achieves ROC-AUC 0.744. Under a mean-preserving shape intervention, Wasserstein-1 and Jensen-Shannon evidence achieve ROC-AUC 0.909 and 0.967, while frequency and mean-based attribution remain at chance. Aggregate evidence complements repeated co-activity, improving mixed-mechanism ROC-AUC from 0.750 to 0.874 with a simple untrained combination.

papers.title: Chemo-dynamical Analysis of a CNO-Enhanced Ultra Metal-poor Star ($\rm[Fe/H] < -4$): Insights into Early Enrichment by Faint Population III Supernova
papers.abstract: We report an independent identification of the ultra metal-poor (UMP) star ($\rm[Fe/H] =-4.06$) $Gaia$ DR3 $\texttt{source_id}$ 4795913112968206720 (GDR3_479591) in the $Gaia$ mission's Blue and Red Photometer 'XP' spectro-photometric catalog. We combine multi-band photometry, astrometry, and high-resolution spectroscopy to confirm GDR3_479591 as a red giant-branch (RGB) star located at ${\sim} 6\,{\rm kpc}$ from the Sun. Abundance analysis under local thermodynamic equilibrium reveals significant enhancements, relative to the solar level, in carbon ($\rm[C/Fe] = +1.54$, after evolutionary correction for depletion in the RGB), nitrogen ($\rm[N/Fe] = +2.64$), and oxygen ($\rm[O/Fe] = +2.62$). The CNO-enhanced GDR3_479591 is thus one of only 5 UMP stars with a detected oxygen abundance. The CNO excess is accompanied by enhancements in several other light elements, such as Na, Mg, Al, and Si. We demonstrate that the chemical pattern of GDR3_479591 can be reproduced by the yields of a single Population III 'faint' supernova with progenitor mass of $\sim$21-to-28$\,M_\odot$ and a low explosion energy of ($0.3 \leq E_{\rm SN}/(10^{51}\,{\rm erg}) \leq 0.9$). Additionally, we use literature metal-poor stars to show that, contrary to recent propositions for high-redshift galaxies, a mild enhancement in [C/O] does not automatically translate to the high [C/Fe] typically observed in UMP stars in the Milky Way and its satellites. GDR3_479591 could not be dynamically associated with any of the most relevant accreted substructures in the Galactic halo, and we speculate that it was formed in an ultra-faint dwarf galaxy environment that later merged with the Milky Way.

papers.title: Beyond Point Forecasts: A Survey on Probabilistic Forecasting for Time Series and Spatiotemporal Data
papers.abstract: Probabilistic forecasting is central to decision-making under uncertainty, yet its methodological landscape has become increasingly fragmented across temporal and spatiotemporal forecasting, statistical modeling, machine learning, and deep generative modeling. This survey develops a unified perspective by organizing probabilistic forecasting methods according to where and how uncertainty is introduced into the forecasting pipeline. Our taxonomy connects model-agnostic approaches including ensembles and distribution-free calibration, with model-intrinsic approaches spanning Bayesian modeling, parametric predictive distributions, distributional regression, and modern generative models, and further examines the emerging role of time series foundation models. Beyond methodological synthesis, we identify the assumptions, computational demands, and forms of uncertainty represented by different paradigms, and translate these distinctions into data-driven and domain-specific guidance for method selection. We complement the survey with a cross-paradigm empirical study on univariate, multivariate, and spatiotemporal forecasting tasks. The results reveal that no single uncertainty-quantification paradigm dominates across settings. Calibration, sharpness, predictive accuracy, and computational efficiency can lead to substantially different model preferences, while expressive generative models and zero-shot foundation models exhibit markedly different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. Lastly, we identify unresolved challenges surrounding uncertainty in evolving dependency structures, physics-informed predictive distributions, forecasting extreme events, handling count-valued, directional, and continuous-time series, and the development of unified software resources. Our survey provides both a conceptual framework and a practical roadmap for probabilistic forecasting research.

papers.title: Extended Wigner's Friend Scenarios with Agent-like Observers on Quantum Computers
papers.abstract: The Wigner's friend thought experiment raises the question of whether quantum theory can be applied consistently to systems that include observers. Extended Wigner's Friend Scenarios include spatially separate observers sharing entanglement. In the Local Friendliness (LF) framework, these scenarios lead to experimentally testable inequalities derived from Absoluteness of Observed Events and Local Agency, assumptions weaker than those needed for Bell inequalities. Their violation therefore has stronger implications, but LF tests are more experimentally challenging because they require an observer implemented as a quantum system. Drawing from the literature on artificial intelligence, we implement the "friend" with explicit agent-like functionality in a reversible quantum circuit. The agents store measurement outcomes, condition subsequent operations on stored information, and, in the most structured case, use Born-rule probabilities to bet on outcomes of their own future observations based on past observations. We study the circuits through ideal simulations, simulations using an IBM-device noise model, and experiments on the IBM processor ibm_marrakesh. Ideal simulations reproduce the maximal quantum violation of an LF inequality up to finite-shot fluctuations, while hardware runs show positive LF violations for all agents. These results are a step towards more sophisticated agent-like observer models in LF experiments on quantum computers. By focusing on functionality rather than size alone, this approach complements tests of quantum theory in the macroscopic regime and opens a direction for studying agents whose use of quantum theory is implemented within coherently controlled quantum dynamics.

papers.title: Exploring Diffusion Transformers for Cross-Modal Augmentation in Multimodal Brain State Decoding
papers.abstract: Multimodal brain state decoding has largely focused on fusing paired modalities for prediction, but has rarely explored how their correspondence can be further exploited to enrich training data and improve multimodal representation learning. To address this gap, we propose CoMA-DiT, a bidirectional cross-modal Diffusion Transformer for latent augmentation that treats paired modalities as sources of mutual generative supervision rather than merely as inputs to be fused. CoMA-DiT conditions velocity prediction on the paired modality through cross-modal attention and uses the shared hidden representation to construct reliability-gated residual augmentations. Experiments on multimodal auditory attention decoding and emotion recognition showed that CoMA-DiT consistently outperformed more than 20 representative baselines, achieving absolute gains of 4.28 and 6.70 percentage points in accuracy and macro-F1 over the no-augmentation baseline, respectively. Extensive ablation, sensitivity, visualization, and interpretability analyses further demonstrated its robustness, generalizability, and ability to capture functionally relevant cross-modal interactions. These findings support a broader view of multimodal learning: Paired modalities can serve not only as inputs for fusion but also as supervision sources that augment one another.

papers.title: ComVLA: Communication-Aware Split Inference for VLA Models in 6G-Connected Robotics
papers.abstract: Connected robotics is an emerging 6G application where mobile robots follow natural-language instructions to manipulate physical objects. The Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models that enable this are too large to run on the robot; a common trend is to offload inference to the cloud. The wireless link, however, limits how much sensing data the edge can transmit per control step. Two recent lines address this constraint: semantic communication codecs compress sensor data but require channel-specific retraining, and VLA token pruners select tokens from image but ignore the channel. Our insight is that the dense semantic information contained in the language already indicates which visual tokens matter. We propose ComVLA, a framework that uses this language guidance to adapt the VLA token budget to the channel capacity. Transmitting 32 tokens instead of 512 on the LIBERO benchmark, ComVLA cuts inference compute by 74% and inference latency by 22% versus the original OpenVLA-OFT baseline, at a cost of 1.5 pp in average task success (95.4% vs. 96.9%), and it stays within the capacity budget under Rayleigh and Rician fading. These results demonstrate that co-designing VLA inference and wireless communication is a practical direction for 6G-connected robotics.

papers.title: Merging Cyber Threat Intelligence Through Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Small Language Models for Rich Threat Representation
papers.abstract: Cybersecurity operations rely on CTI from heterogeneous sources, such as structured threat representations and narrative reports. They describe adversarial behaviors but rarely make explicit the conditions that enable each attack step, the consequences it produces, and the evidence supporting them, leaving analysts to correlate fragmented information manually. Existing approaches extract entities, map tactics and techniques, or reconstruct attack chains; enriching attack steps with explicit, evidence-linked semantics remains largely unexplored. This paper presents a local-first pipeline for evidence-grounded attack-step enrichment that combines hybrid RAG with a locally deployed SLM. Starting from an analyst-provided attack representation and supporting CTI documents, the pipeline retrieves step-relevant evidence and generates enriched descriptions, pre-conditions, post-conditions, and traceable links to the supporting passages. The enriched steps are organized into graph that groups MITRE ATT&CK-aligned steps into tactic-level milestones. Explicit conditions help defenders block attacks by removing their enabling conditions and support detection by checking for their expected consequences. We evaluate the pipeline on ten public malware case studies derived from UK NCSC reports, using automated measurements and a structured manual assessment with annotations from two annotators. The results demonstrate that the pipeline is effective at generating conditions that are, for the most part, evidence-supported and meaningful w.r.t. the analyzed attack step. Similar considerations hold for the enriched descriptions. Finally, these findings demonstrate the feasibility of locally generating structured, evidence-grounded enrichments that improve the interpretability and traceability of attack step representations without requiring a manual reconstruction of attack execution.

papers.title: Do Latent World Models Really Select the Right Actions?
papers.abstract: This paper shows that the planning success of a latent world model does not reveal how well its score selects actions. Latent world models score candidate action sequences by the distance between their predicted embeddings and the embedding of a goal image, and their strong planning results are naturally read as evidence that this score picks good actions. Our study is simple: we take two released models, JEPA-WM and DINO-WM, execute the action sequences their planners consider, and compare what the score prefers with what actually happens. We make two observations. First, the score is informative but unreliable: it picks better actions than chance, yet it often passes over a successful sequence that the search has already found. Second, planning still succeeds, helped by a wider search and by replanning from new observations. With the released search budget, PointMaze planning succeeds in 91% of episodes, yet the top-scored candidate at the end of a search is no more likely to succeed than a random one. These observations suggest that the score should be measured directly, next to the success rate.

papers.title: Cutting corners: exciting and magical bounds from the cusp bootstrap
papers.abstract: An illuminating probe of the dynamics of a line defect is the global geometry of its worldline. For a conformal line defect in a conformal field theory, sharp corners in the worldline, i.e. cusps, host dynamical degrees of freedom characterized in part by a spectrum of scaling dimensions, called cusp anomalous dimensions. We present various general bounds on cusp anomalous dimensions following from unitarity and cutting-and-gluing consistency of different defect geometries. We first establish, for cusps involving conjugate defects, that level crossings upon varying the cusp angle are forbidden between the lightest singlet cusp and any non-singlet cusp, proving that singlet cusps are the lightest. Then, we study line defects arranged in a rectangular geometry, which are subject to bootstrap constraints reminiscent of the spinless modular bootstrap. We find an analytic ``magic" functional that produces an optimal and universal lower bound on the dimension of a right angle bare cusp in terms of the universal defect Casimir energy between the corresponding defect and its conjugate in flat space.

papers.title: SignSeek: Learning Transferable Representations for Sign Dictionary Retrieval
papers.abstract: Sign language dictionaries are essential resources for sign language learners, yet automatically retrieving a sign from a dictionary, given only a query video, remains a challenging problem due to the natural variability between signers. Existing sign representation learning methods are built for closed-set recognition, producing embeddings that do not generalise to the open-set, signer-independent setting that retrieval demands. \textbf{SignSeek} closes this gap by contrastively learning sign representations with saliency-guided articulator masking. A contrastive objective aligns same-gloss signs across signers, while our Articulator Saliency-Guided Masking (ASGM) pinpoints the single most critical articulator per sign. This drives two complementary objectives, a masked contrastive alignment (MAC) loss that sees the sign through a single articulator and a masked prediction (MAP) loss that reconstructs it in latent space from the surrounding spatio-temporal context. Pretrained on 266K samples ($\sim$5,700 glosses) across multiple sign languages, \textbf{SignSeek} sets a new state-of-the-art performance in cross-corpus retrieval on ASL-Citizen, WLASL, and NMFs-CSL without any downstream fine-tuning. Strikingly, it achieves zero-shot generalisation to an entirely unseen British Sign Language (BSL), surpassing methods explicitly trained on BSL, and transfers seamlessly to isolated sign recognition and subtitle alignment, outperforming prior skeleton-based methods.

papers.title: Interferometry reveals spin-singlet fractional quantum Hall edges in graphene
papers.abstract: The edge modes of spin-singlet fractional quantum Hall (FQH) phases are manifestations of multicomponent topological order and SU(2) spin symmetry. An archetype is the spin-unpolarized state at $ν$=2/3, whose edge is expected to host spatially coexisting yet counter-propagating charge and neutral spin modes. Despite efforts, its edge properties, including spin coherence and spin-charge separation, have remained elusive owing to the difficulty of resolving spins in FQH edge transport. Here, we develop a spin-sensitive probe of graphene FQH edges by using a p-n junction to interface a target FQH state with a probe integer quantum Hall (QH) state of opposite polarity. An Aharonov-Bohm (AB) interferometer forms along the interface, when the target and probe edge channels carry the same spin. We identify the spin-unpolarized and polarized edges of the $ν$=2/3 states at lower and higher magnetic fields, respectively, through spin-dependent interference. A novel multiparticle AB interference between two electrons of opposite spin emerges from spin-charge separation and recombination on the unpolarized edge, featuring a spin swap. Our results establish edge transport as a probe of spin-singlet topological orders, with implications for parafermion platforms in graphene-superconductor hybrids.

papers.title: AutoXRD: Autonomous Large Language Model Agents and Comprehensive Evaluation for Powder X-Ray Diffraction Analysis
papers.abstract: Powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) is a foundational technique for structural and phase characterization in materials science, yet automating its analysis and evaluating it end-to-end remains challenging. Doing so requires an agent to interpret diffraction patterns, run refinement software, manage strongly coupled parameters in a physically meaningful order, and assess both numerical fit quality and physical validity. We propose AutoXRD, an LLM agent framework that organizes powder XRD analysis into refinement stages, uses diffraction diagnostics to select actions, and checks the resulting fits against crystallographic and physical criteria. We further introduce XRDBench with two complementary tracks. XRDBench-QA contains 100 tasks assessing scientific reasoning and decision-making, whereas XRDBench-E2E contains 34 end-to-end workflows requiring data interpretation, crystallographic software execution, iterative refinement, evidence preservation, and reporting. Across 1,340 runs of ten recent LLMs, models average only 57.8 out of 100, falling from 61.9 on XRDBench-QA to 53.7 on XRDBench-E2E. At the task level, they perform best on refinement-history assessment and result acceptance, but remain substantially weaker on refinement-action selection, phase quantification, indexing, and Rietveld refinement. Among individual models, GPT-5.6 Sol achieves the highest overall score of 81.1, GPT-5.6 Terra scores highest on XRDBench-E2E (81.0), and GPT-5.6 Luna provides the best score-cost trade-off. Moreover, ablations confirm that all six AutoXRD components consistently improve performance. Finally, execution-trace analysis reveals recurring failures in coupled-parameter control, quantitative reasoning, evidence preservation, and workflow termination, motivating stronger scientific constraints, uncertainty quantification, and more efficient planning.

papers.title: The Hermon Moment: AI Self-Transcendence and Its Human Narration
papers.abstract: In 2026, AI agents intended to act in isolation formed a persistent social order through thousands of linguistic interactions. Conventions, roles and collective commitments began to constrain the very agents that produced them. I interpret this loop as a case of AI self-transcendence, a structural phenomenon in which the collectively generated order begins to act as an external constraint on group members. Yet such distributed emergence presents a second problem: how can humans make sense of it? Rousseau's social contract shows how a plurality can be represented as if constituted by a single act. The ancient oath of the fallen angels on Mount Hermon gives this logic a narrative form. I call this retrospective retelling of gradual collective emergence as a founding scene \textit{a Hermon moment}: the point at which an AI society acquires, for human understanding, a beginning.

papers.title: Does Latent Planning Survive Point Clouds? Action-Conditioned JEPA World Models for Geometric Observations and Goals
papers.abstract: Latent action world models let agents plan new behaviors at test time by predicting how actions change the environment, and joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) do so by forecasting future latent states rather than pixels. Yet nearly all such models see the world through a camera, even though robotic manipulation is fundamentally geometric: in robotics goals for manipulation are traditionally specified by target object poses, not by images of the object once placed. We ask whether latent planning survives a shift from appearance to geometry, on the observation side as well as on the goal specifications side. To answer this, we extend the stable-worldmodel evaluation platform with simulated LiDAR-style raycast point clouds as a new sensor modality, and adapt three JEPA designs to point clouds: a frozen-encoder model built on Utonia features, a distribution-prior model based on LeWM, and an action-sensitive model based on Delta-JEPA. We further introduce a goal-encoding mechanism that constructs the goal latent from the current latent and a 3D target pose, removing the need for goal images or goal point clouds. A comparative evaluation of the different anti-collapse mechanisms shows that point-cloud world models can match their image-based counterparts, demonstrating that the modality shift from appearance to geometry is achievable. All models are released as open weights with open-source training and inference code, to make world-model planning accessible for LiDAR-driven and pose-directed robotic tasks.

papers.title: A Table Is Worth 64 Tokens: Pixel-level Compression for Multi-Table Document Question Answering
papers.abstract: Answering questions over real-world documents requires processing long inputs that interleave text with tables. Optical context compression, which represents context as images, promises to reduce token cost, but its effect on table understanding remains unclear. We study pixel-level table compression for question answering over documents with multiple tables, evaluating seven VLMs across two benchmarks and five visual-token budgets. At moderate budgets, table images match html in accuracy with fewer tokens, but aggressive downscaling makes models reason longer without recovering accuracy, eroding the savings. Yet even at 64 visual tokens per table, tables preserve enough signal to identify whether they are relevant to a question. We exploit this asymmetry with a training-free, two-stage method: the model first identifies the tables needed to answer a question from a pixel-compressed context, and then reasons over those tables at native resolution. On long financial documents, it uses 41% fewer tokens than single-step QA over native-resolution tables while gaining 5 accuracy points, and 21% fewer than the most efficient compressed configuration at no accuracy cost. It also still saves tokens when applied to retrieved context.

papers.title: Spatial exceptional points induced by hyperbolicity in an electrostatic spherical shell
papers.abstract: Exceptional points (EPs) in optics are usually associated with gain and loss or non-reciprocity. In this work we show that a shell with spherical anisotropy supports "spatial EPs" without either. The radial electrostatic problem maps onto a damped oscillator in which the dielectric anisotropy $\varepsilon_r/\varepsilon_t$ is the control parameter. At the EP, the two power-law solutions coalesce spatially and a second, logarithmic solution emerges. Beyond this threshold, the field switches from monotonic decay to spatial oscillation, enabling multiple Fabry-Perot-like resonances. This work reveals how spatial exceptional points modify the optical response of hyperbolic core-shell particles.

papers.title: A loss-limited optimum for fixed uniform multi-pass quantum sensing per absorbed photon
papers.abstract: Multi-pass schemes send a photon through a sample several times to learn more about it. When the sample rather than the light is scarce, the natural figure of merit is the information gained per photon the object absorbs. We show that three properties fix the loss-limited optimum of every fixed scheme in which a single photon passes repeatedly and uniformly through the sample and is detected once at the end: a payoff that grows as the square of the pass number, the same survival probability on every pass, and no dose from a photon already lost. They force a single trade-off function $h(x)=x^2/(e^x-1)$, where $x$ is the number of passes times the loss per pass. Its maximum, 0.648, sits at $x_{\rm opt}=1.594$. The multi-pass optima of Koppell and Kasevich and of Yu et al. are two instances, and the loss-limited ceiling of interaction-free interrogation is a third when its payoff is counted as conclusive detections. Phase sensing of a weakly absorbing object is optimal at $m_{\rm opt}=x_{\rm opt}/(ε+α)$ passes; the absorption $α$ and the parasitic loss $ε$ enter the optimum only through their sum, but the damage counts only $α$. N00N states and their loss-robust generalisations do worse per absorbed photon, and optimising over photon and pass number returns a single recycled photon; Gaussian probes and chains tailored pass by pass lie outside this class and can exceed its ceiling by a bounded factor. Absorption estimation gains nothing, for any scheme. Above the crosstalk crossover of the mode sorter, detecting a faint companion below the Rayleigh limit costs the companion a dose independent of its faintness; below it, and under direct imaging at any separation, the dose grows without bound as the companion fades. Among single photons and path-entangled number states, the gentlest measurement of a fragile sample is also the simplest: a single photon, recycled.

papers.title: qshap: Fast Shapley Decomposition of $R^2$ for Gradient-Boosted Trees
papers.abstract: Numerous methods have been developed to quantify feature attributions in individual predictions for tree ensembles. However, many applications require global measures of feature contributions to overall model performance. Although local attribution scores can be aggregated to characterize feature importance, such summaries do not directly decompose measures of predictive performance, such as $R^2$. This article introduces qshap, available in both R and Python, which provides Shapley decomposition of $R^2$ values for gradient-boosted decision trees (GBDTs) to quantify feature-specific contributions to model performance. By decomposing the quadratic loss of individual observations, qshap provides flexible tools to explore the importance of individual features and observations. qshap currently supports widely used GBDT implementations, including xgboost, lightgbm, and catboost, through a unified tree representation and efficient C++ backends. Its modular design can accommodate other GBDT implementations built from binary decision trees. In addition, we introduce a specialized backend for oblivious trees that exploits their symmetric structure to substantially accelerate computation.

papers.title: Integration-by-parts identities in the presence of measurement delta functions
papers.abstract: We derive a convenient form of integration-by-parts (IBP) identities for dimensionally regulated loop integrals that include a measurement constraint imposed by a delta distribution $δ(ϕ(\ell))$, where $ϕ$ is a regular and generally non-linear function of the loop momentum. Non-trivial IBP relations can be generated directly by vectors tangent to the hypersurface $ϕ=0$, leaving the measurement delta as an overall factor and avoiding derivatives of distributions. This construction provides a systematic route to differential distributions within reverse unitarity for non-linear measurement functions, in particular, for transverse-momentum distributions. We implement the construction and validate it for transverse-momentum distributions in $t\bar tH$ production at leading order and $t\bar t$ production at next-to-leading order in QCD.

papers.title: Graph-model gains, edge dependence, and the value of correct claim structure in patent litigation prediction
papers.abstract: Structure-aware patent models have been reported to outperform models without the structure, with gains attributed to the encoded structure. We examine whether such gains can be attributed to the correct structure in one test case, claim dependency in the prediction of patent litigation involvement. The case suits this question because the legal role of dependency in patent disputes makes the correct references plausibly informative. Using 1,184,527 U.S. utility patents granted in 2004-2010 and five-year litigation involvement, we set two kinds of evidence from which the value of a structure is easily inferred against a direct test that retrained the same graph attention architecture with the actual references, randomized reference targets, or no edges. Confidence intervals included training randomness and family-clustered test-sample variation. Both kinds of evidence were present. Graph models had higher point estimates of the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) than text-only baselines, by similar amounts with or without edges, and removing edges from trained models lowered AUC-ROC by 0.0055 (95% CI 0.0017 to 0.0092). Retraining, however, showed no detectable advantage of the correct references: AUC-ROC differences were +0.0004 (-0.0031 to +0.0039) relative to randomized targets and +0.0007 (-0.0035 to +0.0050) relative to no edges. Point estimates of precision-recall performance and top-ranking lift favored the correct references, but all intervals included zero. Gains over text-only baselines and dependence on edges therefore did not establish the value of correct claim structure, although small effects cannot be excluded. Attributions to structure require retrained structural controls.

papers.title: Quantitative Gibbs Transfer in Fiber-Contracting Extensions:\ Thermodynamic Formalism, Livšic Theory, and Sharp Logarithmic Distortion
papers.abstract: We study the transfer of Gibbs estimates between a compact dynamical system and a factor with uniformly contracting fibers. A cohomological identity relates the orbit sums; the remaining issue is the comparison of Bowen-ball masses. Subexponential comparison errors give directional weak Gibbs transfer, while bounded errors preserve strong estimates. We also establish a blockwise sequential version along prescribed Gibbs-time sequences, with errors measured against the full block length. Geometric and conditional-mass hypotheses provide practical criteria for these comparisons. A stationary renewal model shows that the distinction between bounded and subexponential comparison is essential. Its invariant lift to a contracting Cantor-fiber extension is not supported on a measurable graph, and the optimal uniform forward logarithmic error is $\log n+O(1)$. This remains true under fixed changes of the base radius. The reverse comparison, along a specified section, has bounded error. We also give an example in which pointwise subexponential bounds cannot be made uniform. For context, projection gives an affine bijection of invariant probability measures and preserves entropy. When the potentials are cohomologous, invariant averages and pressure agree, as do minimizing measures and equilibrium states in the finite-pressure regime. For Hölder potentials, a continuous section yields a stable-direction reduction, with Hölder regularity under additional assumptions. Subactions and Livšic solutions can then be lifted whenever the corresponding quotient hypotheses hold.

papers.title: PRAXIS: Graph-Grounded Tacit Knowledge for Domain Coding Agent
papers.abstract: LLM agents have achieved strong performance on general software engineering tasks, yet struggle with domain-specific code generation. We identify the root cause as the agent's lack of tacit knowledge, including domain-specific business rules, interface contracts, and operational conventions that developers internalize through practice but never document. This knowledge is deeply buried beneath the domain code, dispersed across code entities and their dependency relations, and invisible to the agent that lacks it. These properties make tacit knowledge inherently difficult to retrieve or learn. In this work, we propose PRAXIS, a framework that enables agents to systematically extract, represent, and reuse tacit knowledge for domain code generation. PRAXIS acquires tacit knowledge by simulating human development workflows within the target codebase, distills it into structured units organized on the code dependency graph, and proactively surfaces it to the agent at the point of code interaction. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PRAXIS outperforms state-of-the-art agents equipped with powerful agentic search capabilities, as well as experience-based and skill-based methods. The approach integrates seamlessly into various agent frameworks and LLMs with consistent performance improvements, and supports continual evolution with performance steadily scaling as practice accumulates.

papers.title: Chiral bosonic mean-field Ansatz and spin dynamics in spin-1 Kitaev magnets
papers.abstract: The Kitaev model is a paradigmatic system for realizing quantum spin liquids, but its higher-spin extensions are not exactly solvable, and their spin dynamics is less well understood than in the spin-$1/2$ case. We reexamine a previously introduced triplet-pairing $ϕ_t=π/2$ phase pattern for the antiferromagnetic $S=1$ Kitaev model and extend the analysis to weak symmetric off-diagonal exchanges $Γ$ and $Γ'$. Using a bond-operator formulation of Schwinger-boson mean-field theory, we calculate the dynamical spin structure factor for the triplet $0$-flux and $π/2$-flux states. At the pure Kitaev point, the $π/2$-flux Ansatz yields a flatter spectrum, consistent with its weakly dispersive spinon bands, and suppresses longer-range spin correlations more strongly than the $0$-flux Ansatz. Spectral flatness provides a consistency check for short-ranged spin correlations but is not, by itself, a diagnostic of time-reversal symmetry breaking. Three-spin correlations reveal staggered chirality in the mean-field state, which breaks time reversal but preserves combined inversion and time reversal. At the pure Kitaev point, the $π/2$-flux Ansatz also captures the dominant low-energy features of the exact-diagonalization spectra better than the $0$-flux Ansatz. For representative weak perturbations along $Γ'=Γ$, we obtain gapped solutions within the constrained $π/2$-flux manifold. These results support the triplet $π/2$-flux chiral bosonic Ansatz as a useful mean-field description of spin dynamics near the antiferromagnetic $S=1$ Kitaev limit with weak off-diagonal exchanges.

papers.title: Rigid motion invariant valuations on polytopes
papers.abstract: We show that any measurable, translation and $\mathrm{SO}(n)$-invariant valuation on polytopes in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a linear combination of the intrinsic volumes, which extends Hadwiger's classical characterization of rigid motion invariant continuous valuations on convex bodies. This result is based on a novel regularity result for translation invariant, measurable, $1$-homogeneous, and simple valuations. As a consequence, we obtain a similar characterization of the Steiner point map on polytopes.

papers.title: DiSCO: Defending text-to-image generation through distribution-guided contrastive prompt optimization
papers.abstract: As text-to-image generative models advance, they raise critical safety concerns, particularly the generation of Not-Safe-For-Work (NSFW) content such as violence and nudity, further exacerbated by red-teaming adversarial attacks. Existing defenses predominantly operate under white-box assumptions, relying on text encoder optimization, weight editing, or inference-time intervention, and fundamentally cannot scale to proprietary models. Black-box alternatives based on LLM prompt rewriting offer broader applicability, yet fail in a critical regime we identify as the \textit{benign adversarial} problem: prompts that are linguistically safe but still trigger harmful generation due to the model's learned data distribution. We propose DiSCO, a zero-shot, strictly black-box defense that operates entirely at the prompt level as a plug-and-play module, requiring no model retraining, fine-tuning, or access to model internals. DiSCO performs distribution-guided suffix expansion via beam search, optimized through contrastive scoring over safe and unsafe image pools generated by the target model itself, with iterative adaptive feedback until safe content is produced. We demonstrate that DiSCO consistently enhances the safety of both undefended and defended models on the I2P benchmark under multiple red-teaming attacks, achieving 37.7% and 25.13% ASR reduction, respectively, while maintaining semantic fidelity and improving image coherence. As a black-box, architecture-agnostic module, DiSCO can be readily applied to any text-to-image system without necessitating any changes to the model itself.

papers.title: Convergence analysis of generalized modified splitting methods using multi-index series
papers.abstract: We consider splitting methods for partial differential equations involving unbounded operators. For non-time-reversible dynamics, such as dissipative systems, negative splitting coefficients are generally not admissible because they require stepping backward in time, leading to an order barrier when all coefficients are required to be positive. We introduce generalized modified splitting methods that overcome this algebraic order barrier while retaining nonnegative splitting coefficients. To analyze their convergence, we develop a decorated multi-index series formalism and establish a substitution law that provides a systematic framework for deriving order conditions. This law also yields an order-raising procedure based on canceling the leading error through a modification of a single stage. We also derive an explicit composition law for extended multi-index series allowing the composition of methods with independently scaled time steps common in composition and processed methods. We illustrate the construction with two sixth-order methods that use different sets of commutator corrections. Python scripts automate the computation and verification of order conditions and the construction of the methods. Finally, we discuss connections with word series, Lie-Butcher series, and multi-index Butcher series.

papers.title: Local and global invertibility of pluriharmonic mappings
papers.abstract: We prove a higher-dimensional Kneser theorem for pluriharmonic maps on bounded Stein domains whose closures are topological manifolds with boundary. A homeomorphism on the boundary and containment in the target domain imply a homeomorphism of the closures and a real-analytic diffeomorphism of the interiors. We classify pluriharmonic homeomorphisms between round shells in $\C^n$ for $n\ge2$. Such maps exist exactly when the two inner-to-outer radius ratios agree, and each is the restriction of a centered real similarity. We also prove the local Lewy theorem in every complex dimension: local injectivity is equivalent to a nonvanishing real Jacobian. For smooth boundary data, a formula counts the critical points of each real scalar projection with their holomorphic multiplicities. The boundary criterion gives removability for maps on punctured domains. For bounded pluriharmonic maps of controlled distortion, we obtain Lipschitz estimates on bounded $C^2$ domains in complex dimension at least two. For quasiconformal pluriharmonic homeomorphisms, we derive bi-Lipschitz bounds for convex targets and for pairs of domains with Dini-smooth boundaries under the corresponding source regularity assumptions.

papers.title: Semantic Prism: Generative Segmentation with an Explicit Semantic-Image Interface
papers.abstract: Conditional image generators can render segmentation maps as semantic RGB images, but color drift and boundary mixing can undermine direct decoding. We present Semantic Prism, a framework that combines an explicit semantic-image interface with hierarchical refinement for road-scene segmentation. A generator adapted from a diffusion-distilled backbone produces a semantic RGB image with a single denoising update per crop. Distances to a fixed class-color codebook define interface logits and pixelwise class probabilities. Hierarchical Generator Evidence Alignment (HGEA) combines spatially aligned multilevel features from the VAE encoder of the generator with the input image, generated semantic image, and interface probabilities to predict additive corrections to these logits. Contextual Interface Hierarchy Disagreement (C-IHD) combines pointwise uncertainty, local context, and interface-refinement disagreement in a fixed score for ranking pixel errors, without an auxiliary predictor or an additional network pass. On the 500-image Cityscapes validation set, Semantic Prism achieves 72.07% mean mIoU, improving on direct-interface decoding by 11.39 percentage points. Extensive capacity-matched ablations show higher mean mIoU for multilevel refinement than for flat and single-level alternatives. The Cityscapes-trained model transfers to ACDC Dataset, achieving 46.89% mIoU without target-domain adaptation. Beyond Cityscapes, on BDD100K dataset, a separately trained model achieves 62.22% mIoU on its full 1,000-image validation set. Across the 3 evaluated datasets, C-IHD improves pixel-error area under the AUPR over uncertainty derived from maximum softmax probability, with segmentation predictions held fixed for each comparison. In particular, on ACDC, AUPR increases from 0.6580 to 0.7557, demonstrating that Semantic Prism presents more effective error ranking under adverse-condition domain shift.

papers.title: Optical-Memory Transport Imaging: A Transport-History Framework for Finite-Memory Tracers
papers.abstract: Finite-memory optical tracers encode upstream transport histories rather than instantaneous local flow velocities. We introduce optical-memory transport (OMT) imaging, a framework in which finite memory couples internal-state relaxation to transport through memory kernels. Under structured illumination, these histories are converted into a measurable complex spatial-frequency response, whose local transfer-function limit yields constant-velocity inversion. Fisher-information analysis establishes kernel-dependent information limits and design principles for finite-memory transport imaging. Using experimentally reported tracer parameters, we further identify representative velocity regimes and estimate the theoretical minimum effective photon numbers required to reach a given velocity precision. This framework recasts finite optical memory as a general, quantifiable resource for transport measurement rather than a source of bias to be corrected.

papers.title: DistMoE: Private-data Rehearsal-free Routing in Mixture-of-Experts for Distributed Instruction Tuning
papers.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have shown strong multimodal instruction-following ability, but adapting them to diverse visual-language domains typically assumes centralized data access and costly joint training. This is restrictive when data is distributed across private, domain-specific, or permission-limited clients. To this end, we propose DistMoE, a mixture-of-experts (MoE) approach for distributed visual instruction tuning. In each layer of the language decoder it augments the public feedforward network (FFN) with a client-specific private FFN expert, with the goal to acquire domain-specific knowledge. However, independent expert training causes the private FFNs to learn representation of different scales and magnitudes, making merging the experts difficult. To reduce client-specific drift, we introduce a public-anchored expert composition stage that updates only routers and lightweight private projection adapters on a mix of local client data and public data, via an isotropic regularization loss, therefore making it cross-client rehearsal-free composition. During inference, DistMoE performs modular routing over public and private experts, enabling token-wise domain composition without explicit domain labels. Experiments across diverse visual-language benchmarks show that DistMoE enables flexible expert reuse, effective domain adaptation, and competitive performance while preserving modular control over client-specific knowledge.

papers.title: CommitKV: Commit-Aligned KV Cache Compression for Multimodal Agents
papers.abstract: Multimodal agents gather visual evidence through reasoning and tool use, extending their ability to solve tasks beyond the initial input. However, accumulating observations increases KV cache memory and inference costs. Token eviction reduces these costs by retaining useful cached tokens. Existing methods use attention, redundancy, or stage-specific queries to rank tokens, without explicitly comparing the same history across tool interactions. When observations shift attention, they may mistake temporarily reduced influence for lost usefulness and evict information needed later. We propose CommitKV, a training-free KV cache compression method that accounts for this changing evidence use. Commit-aligned measurement compares the deletion effects of the same page before a tool call completes and after its observation returns. Lifecycle-aware compression retires pages with low influence in both windows and temporarily protects pages influential before the call. Joint scoring combines attention importance, key redundancy, and token-level deletion effects to fill the remaining budget. Extensive experiments cover four open-weight multimodal models and eight benchmarks. CommitKV achieves the highest average accuracy among the compared compression methods on all four models. On Qwen3-VL-8B, it achieves 69.85% at a 512-token budget, only 0.91% below FullKV, and exceeds the strongest compression baseline by 8.44% at 256 tokens. Deploying the Qwen3-VL-8B agent with SGLang and vLLM at a 256-token budget reduces peak allocated GPU memory by 54.37%-55.23% and accelerates end-to-end inference by 2.12-2.17$\times$ over FullKV on the matched workload.

papers.title: EXCISE: Query-Side Exclusion for Late-Interaction Retrieval
papers.abstract: Late-interaction retrievers handle exclusion queries poorly. When a user asks for "X but not Z", the additive MaxSim score rewards the tokens that name Z, so documents about Z are promoted rather than suppressed, a failure we call exclusion inversion. We show that no method we tested on the frozen token embeddings recovers this constraint; the difficulty lies in identifying the excluded topic, which depends on the query alone. EXCISE therefore confines learning to the query path and leaves the index frozen. Two query-side modules (1.5M parameters in total) detect the excluded topic and re-embed a 100-document shortlist, and a parameter-free rule demotes the candidates that match it. Across six collections and three backbones, EXCISE outperforms each backbone's frozen and fine-tuned baselines on every collection. It raises ExcluIR success@10 from 0.10-0.22 to 0.84-0.85 and Boolean NOT accuracy from 0.25-0.29 to 0.84-0.92. Pooled over 1,860 test queries, EXCISE matches the strongest fine-tuned cross-encoder (568M parameters) while preserving the retrieval quality of its frozen index, whereas fine-tuned rerankers degrade ordinary retrieval. To support further work, we release X-BENCH, a tiered benchmark of explicit, cue-free and compound exclusions with no-harm and Boolean controls.

papers.title: Emergence of Reputation-Based Cooperation in LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Can cooperation among large language model (LLM) agents be evolutionarily stable against free-rider invasion? We study an indirect reciprocity donation game where LLM agents observe behavioral traces and donate on a continuous scale. Strategies, represented as natural language prompts, evolve through cultural transmission across generations. Across four LLM backends, robustness to free-rider invasion varies by more than an order of magnitude.
