Recent developments in artificial intelligence (AI) technologies have opened up new opportunities for more rapid, iterative, and responsive mapping of relevant evidence to support such early-stage evidence-to-policy dialogues and processes. In this article, we outline and characterise this emerging approach, termed Rapid Exploratory Maps (REMs). We also present two illustrative case studies drawn from first-hand experiences within a programme of evidence reviews production to inform government policy in England. While this approach could be transformative for the mapping process, its broader potential is as yet largely unassessed, and it confers important challenges and likely risks, as well as benefits. Determining whether REMs could usefully support more efficient ways of working with end users when developing and designing evidence syntheses will require continued development and careful evaluation.

papers.title: Compositional Symbolic Execution à la Carte (Extended Version)
papers.abstract: We introduce compositional symbolic execution à la carte, a modular approach for building compositional symbolic execution (CSE) tools, powered by combinator-based design of key components, including memory models, management and automation of user-defined predicates, and bi-abductive analysis. Our approach is grounded on meta-theory mechanised in the Rocq proof assistant and allows tool developers to easily build correct-by-construction CSE tools for symbolic analysis of their programming languages of choice, with minimal implementation and proof effort. We show how our approach scales to real-world languages by implementing it in Gillian, a state-of-the-art CSE tool, and using it to capture the intricacies of the memory models of C, JavaScript, and Rust. We evaluate our approach by running all of the relevant previous case studies of Gillian, showing no unexpected behaviours and comparable performance.

papers.title: Heights and energies of polarized fibrations of varieties II. Fibrations over a polarized base
papers.abstract: We extend the height and energy inequalities for fibrations over curves to a fibration $f:X\to Y$ over a polarized variety $(Y,B)$. For an integrable relatively nef adelic line bundle $\bar L$, we prove a height inequality under the assumption that $L$ is nef on the inverse image of a geometric generic complete-intersection curve in $Y$. We deduce a lower bound for the local energy at almost every complex or nonarchimedean realization of a fixed polarized model when $L$ is $f$-ample. For a slope semistable bundle on a fixed polarized complex variety, we show that the infimum of the energy on its projective bundle equals the infimum of Donaldson's functional on Hermitian quotient metrics, with the normalization given below.

papers.title: GRUN: Generalized Retinex Unfolding Network for Image Restoration
papers.abstract: Image restoration remains a fundamental challenge in low-level vision, requiring methods that handle diverse degradations while preserving scene structures and details. We revisit classical Retinex theory and propose a Generalized Retinex formulation that extends the illumination-reflectance decomposition into a Retinex-inspired content-environment factorization prior for image restoration. The key idea is to restore images using two learned factors: a content-dominant response (generalized reflectance) capturing scene properties and an environment-side response (generalized illumination) encoding task-dependent variations associated with the observed degradations. Based on this formulation, we develop GRUN (Generalized Retinex Unfolding Network), a MAP-guided deep unfolding framework that alternates reflectance restoration, illumination estimation, and progressive degradation inference across K stages with degradation-conditioned proximal operators. We further introduce a Degradation-aware Coupling Regularizer (DCR) that combines mutual information minimization, gradient decorrelation, and scale anchoring to promote complementary content-environment factor representations. Experiments on seven image restoration tasks, including denoising, dehazing, deraining, low-light enhancement, deblurring, underwater enhancement, and backlit enhancement, demonstrate competitive results on multiple benchmarks using the same architecture with task-specific weights. Moreover, the proposed Generalized Retinex design can be integrated into existing restoration methods, demonstrating its cross-architecture applicability. Code will be released.

papers.title: GeoMVGen: Joint Appearance-Geometry Modeling for Multi-View Video Generation in Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Robotic manipulation requires predicting how robot-object interactions evolve over time, encompassing both visual appearance and scene geometry. In multi-camera settings, such predictions need to capture the evolving 3D scene consistently across viewpoints, while supporting controllable generation under different robot actions and camera configurations. Existing video generation models provide strong priors for visual appearance and motion but typically lack explicit geometric modeling. Meanwhile, recent advances in geometry-aware and multi-view generation have explored joint appearance-geometry modeling and cross-view consistency, yet generating temporally coherent appearance and geometry across multiple viewpoints under robotic manipulation conditions remains challenging. In this work, we propose GeoMVGen, a framework for joint multi-view RGB and pointmap video generation in robotic manipulation. Built on a video diffusion transformer, our framework employs modality-specific adaptation modules to capture the distinct characteristics of appearance and geometry, while using cross-modal residual connections to facilitate information exchange between the two modalities. To establish geometric correspondences across viewpoints, we further introduce a cross-view projection mechanism with complementary geometric supervisions, combining pointmap consistency with geometry foundation model-guided feature alignment. These designs enable controllable generation of temporally evolving multi-view observations with coherent appearance and geometrically consistent scene structures. Extensive experiments on 4D video generation dataset comprising simulated and real-world robotic manipulation scenarios demonstrate that GeoMVGen outperforms state-of-the-art methods in video quality, geometric accuracy, and cross-view consistency.

papers.title: Harvesting Apple's Orchard: A Security Analysis of On-Device CoreML Models Across the Apple Ecosystem
papers.abstract: Apple ships hundreds of task-specific machine-learning models inside iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and tvOS. We present, to our knowledge, the first systematic security analysis of this on-device surface. We harvested 1,137 CoreML artifacts from six platform images and two device harvests, and a conversion pipeline recovered 155 previously opaque bundles as loadable mlpackage archives. Eight findings. (1) 368 of 1,137 artifacts expose plaintext learned parameters (281 blobs, 369.61 MiB) and 166 of 166 MIL bundles leak internal model-database tokens. (2) Specification versions 1-9 coexist and locale variants diverge architecturally. (3) Across 82,092 adversarial evaluations (221 model paths), worst-case flip rates reach 100%; zero-width spaces flip 65% of the Indian-English and 70% of the US-English SMS filter. (4) A 16-byte weight edit flips 7 of 8 probe inputs of a system model, with no runtime integrity check observed. (5) Loading Apple's own hand-gesture model crashes libBNNS through the public CoreML API (4/4 on production M2, also macOS 27.0); Apple ruled it a self-crash outside the security boundary. (6) Eleven bundles ship isUpdatable=1 hooks. (7) SMS text-classifier latency is 13.1-52.0 ms, 92.4% in the CPU-side NLP core, not the ANE. (8) The classifiers label 8-9 of 10 phishing messages Transactional. We filed three reports with Apple Product; all were declined as not crossing a security boundary, and we report the findings as robustness results.

papers.title: Online Statistical Inference for Derivative-Free Constrained Stochastic Optimization
papers.abstract: We study statistical inference for nonlinear equality-constrained stochastic optimization problems in settings where derivative information is unavailable or expensive to obtain. While recent advances in stochastic sequential quadratic programming (SSQP) have enabled efficient online optimization, existing methods either rely on gradient information or suffer from high computational costs. To address these limitations, we develop a sketched derivative-free SSQP (SDF-SSQP) method that simultaneously achieves computational efficiency and valid statistical inference. By leveraging randomized sketching, the proposed method reduces the per-iteration computational cost to $O((d+m)^2)$, where $d$ is the dimension of the decision variable and $m$ is the number of constraints, making it well suited for large-scale problems. To overcome the challenges that both sketching and zeroth-order approximations introduce for statistical inference, we adopt a random-scaling approach that eliminates the need for explicit estimation of the asymptotic covariance matrix. We establish the asymptotic normality of the averaged primal--dual iterates and construct a self-normalized statistic that is asymptotically pivotal. The resulting inference procedure is fully online, requires neither covariance estimation nor matrix inversion, and incurs an additional per-iteration cost of the same order as that of the optimization update. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in terms of both optimization performance and statistical inference accuracy.

papers.title: Right Destination, Wrong Journey: Synthetic Counseling Dialogues Miss Human Interactional Dynamics
papers.abstract: LLM-generated counseling dialogues are increasingly used for training and evaluating mental-health systems, yet existing evaluations focus largely on response quality and final outcomes rather than how support unfolds over time. We conduct a trajectory-centered evaluation of process fidelity across ten human, reconstructed, and synthetic counseling datasets. Our results show that synthetic dialogues often reach plausible endpoints but differ from human support in recovery dynamics and turn-by-turn responsiveness. While generation design can shift global properties such as recovery timing and trajectory structure, contingent patient--counselor responsiveness remains consistently lower in fidelity across models and generation paradigms. Our experiments on controlled synthetic datasets show that targeted generation interventions can narrow the gap with real data on several trajectory-level measures, but do not fully recover interactional fidelity, with turn-level responsiveness remaining limited. We release three controlled synthetic datasets comprising 2,050 dialogues, together with annotations and the evaluation framework.

papers.title: A Constant-Factor Single-Sample Prophet Inequality for Subadditive Valuations
papers.abstract: We establish a constant-factor single-sample prophet inequality for online combinatorial allocation with monotone subadditive valuations. Given one independent sample from each buyer's unknown distribution, our reduction converts any offline algorithm achieving an $α$ fraction of optimal welfare into an online algorithm achieving an $α/120$ fraction of the expected offline optimum. The guarantee holds for arbitrary arrival orders and extends to the stronger Game of Googol model. Our approach has two key ingredients: a prior-free random score generator and a new sample-based construction of tentative allocations. The tentative allocations capture substantial welfare while controlling contention for items, and the score generator relates itemwise competition in the tentative allocations to the value of retained bundles. The reduction is efficient whenever its offline allocator and score generator are efficient.

papers.title: CROSS-Calib: Selective Channel Calibration for Ultrasound Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Ultrasound imaging provides views of internal tissue in real time for medical diagnosis. However, ultrasound signals may be affected by interference, and correcting errors and removing transient interference while preserving valid echoes remains challenging. We propose CROSS-Calib, a channel recovery method that uses predictions from other channels as references for amplitude and phase calibration, while a gate using context selectively combines calibrated measurements with predicted echoes to retain usable samples and repair unreliable ones. On the in vivo test set, CROSS-Calib outperforms all baseline models under gain errors and transient interference, while phantom tests show that the model restores cyst contrast with echo widths of wire targets close to the clean reference. CROSS-Calib can perform channel calibration and selective repair before beamforming to improve echo usability and image quality.

papers.title: The local intertwining relation for inner forms of $\mathrm{GL}_N$
papers.abstract: The local intertwining relation for inner forms of general linear groups over a local field asserts that the normalized intertwining operator for every parabolically induced representation arising from a local A-parameter is the identity operator. Our main theorem verifies the claim over local fields of characteristic zero. This will serve as a vital ingredient for completing the local intertwining relation and endoscopic classification for non-quasi-split unitary groups.

papers.title: LimoBench: How Street Smart Are Large Language Models?
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have transformed how humans interact with information, enabling natural-language interfaces across various domains. They are increasingly deployed for geospatial applications including map-based question answering, location-based services, and natural-language interfaces to spatial databases. But are LLMs truly location-aware, able to reliably interpret and precisely answer location queries involving real-world coordinates, points of interest (POIs), and geospatial distances? To answer this concretely, we present LimoBench, a street-level benchmark of 82 natural-language location queries over seven canonical spatial operations: geocoding, reverse geocoding, routing, directionality, range search, $k$-nearest-neighbor search, and spatial join. The queries are grounded in real map data of West Lafayette, Indiana, and are graded by location and semantic complexity. They are designed to probe LLMs' street-level spatial awareness, from simple lookups to multi-step spatial reasoning. We also present Limo, an approach based on the Model Context Protocol (MCP) that enhances the location awareness of LLMs. Limo grounds LLMs in PostGIS-backed spatial data through a compact set of tools. We find that ungrounded models mostly achieve single-digit accuracy (3.1% for GPT-6 Luna) across different spatial operations. In contrast, the same models achieve near-perfect accuracy (99.3% for GPT-6 Luna) when given access to Limo's spatial tools through MCP. Current LLMs thus have limited and unreliable street-level spatial knowledge, while grounding provides accurate answers at modest overhead (+0.2 s latency, 7.7$\times$ tokens, and 2.2$\times$ cost for GPT-6 Luna). We release the benchmark, Limo toolset, and evaluation code to encourage the community to evaluate their own location-aware LLM approaches.

papers.title: Your bids are showing: re-identifying power plants in anonymized market data, and a differentially private alternative
papers.abstract: ERCOT publishes every generator's hourly offer curve 60 days after the operating day. Market monitors, researchers and traders use these records to study the merit order and check for withholding. PJM publishes the same kind of data with unit names replaced by codes, on the view that masking keeps offers confidential. We test that view on ERCOT data from 2024 to 2026, where names are public and so provide ground truth, by masking the records under PJM's published rules. Public EIA and EPA data match 25% of the masked units we can score (32% of their capacity) to their plant, and 45% fall within the top five guesses. PJM's feed carries the same fields, so we expect masking to fail there too. Publishing exact fuel-group totals instead does not help. An attacker who knows the other units in a group recovers one unit's high-price offers exactly, and an outsider who knows only the target's outage dates reaches a correlation of 0.77, most of it from a few renewable and hydro units that offer at very high prices (0.32 over fossil units). We propose a differentially private release: monthly totals by fuel group and price bin, with Gaussian noise calibrated under zero-concentrated differential privacy so that each unit's whole year of offers is protected. It publishes an unbiased noisy layer and derives a monotone supply curve and shares from it at no extra privacy cost. At $\varepsilon=10$ per unit-year the market supply curve stays within 11% of the truth, the implied clearing price within \$3.0/MWh, and the attacker's correlation falls to 0.23. Whether an analysis still works depends on one ratio, how much the true quantity varies month to month against the noise, which predicts the accuracy of totals to within 0.05. The clearing price, supply slope and combined-cycle capacity remain usable, but no monthly release, private or exact, can answer questions about single hours or single units.

papers.title: Curvature-Equilibrated Policy Optimization for Deep Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Gradient-based actor optimization is central to deep reinforcement learning. However, conventional first-order optimizers do not explicitly exploit the local curvature of neural actor losses. We propose EQUIP (Curvature-Equilibrated Gradients for Policy Search), a novel approach that seeks to balance local contraction and expansion of the actor parameter space by equilibrating positive and negative curvature. EQUIP constructs a trajectory-informed search subspace and uses the projected Hessian of actor loss to build a bounded local metric for curvature equilibration. First-order loss matching preserves the approximated first-order decrease in actor loss. Meanwhile, gradient mixing and curvature-based gradient selection adjust the gradient applied for actor optimization. We establish the geometric properties of curvature equilibration, derive bounds on gradient alignment and magnitude, and identify conditions for improved actor loss reduction and convergence toward stationarity under direct gradient updates. We integrate EQUIP into Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) without modifying its actor loss, critic learning, or replay mechanism. Experiments on 6 MuJoCo continuous control benchmarks show that the resulting EQUIP-SAC algorithm achieves higher mean sample efficiency than SAC and two second-order policy optimization baselines. Ablation studies further highlight the benefits of curvature equilibration and trajectory-informed geometry for policy training.

papers.title: Rethinking Document Indexing for LLM-based Analysis
papers.abstract: Documents such as clinical records, legal contracts, and scientific papers are increasingly analyzed with large language models (LLMs). The naïve approach of prompting the model with the full text for every question is slow, expensive, prone to hallucination on long inputs, and reuses no work across questions. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems build reusable state to address this, but they store it as embedded chunks: slicing text into fragments can lose the meaning that spans them, and the resulting index is tied to one embedding model, so it must be rebuilt whenever that model changes. Answering many questions over a large body of data without a full rescan, however, is not a new problem: it is the problem database indexes have been solving for decades, and we argue that this accumulated index design knowledge is waiting to be revisited for LLM access. As a concrete starting point, we propose Periplus, a hierarchical plain-text index inspired by the classic B+ tree. It arranges a document into pages running from general summaries at the root to specific ones at the leaves, so that each level guides the search into the next. But it departs from the B+ tree in three ways suited to LLM access: content lives at every level, the pages are plain text rather than attribute values, and navigation follows the relevance of a page summary to the question rather than a key comparison. The structure itself is discovered per document by the LLM rather than hand-designed in advance. In a preliminary evaluation on narrative and contract corpora, Periplus comes within 0.1--0.9 percentage points of the strongest baseline's accuracy while consuming 70--72\% fewer total tokens. These early results are encouraging, and they offer only a glimpse of what index design can bring to LLM-based analysis.

papers.title: $AdS$ Leading Regge Trajectory from String Field Theory
papers.abstract: We determine the $AdS$ mass of the leading Regge trajectory in superstring backgrounds $AdS_5\times S^5$, $AdS_4\times\mathbb{CP}^3$, and $AdS_3\times S^3\times{\cal M}_4$ with pure Ramond-Ramond (RR) flux for both ${\cal M}_4=S^3\times S^1$ and ${\cal M}_4=T^4$, to the second order in the expansion with respect to the background RR flux by solving the linearized equations of motion in closed superstring field theory. The $AdS_5$ and $AdS_4$ results are in a complete agreement with those obtained from the integrability approach to dual gauge theories, thereby providing a nontrivial check of the holographic duality beyond supersymmetry-protected quantities.

papers.title: Look Before You Commit: Visual-Evidence-Guided Decoding for Multimodal Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract: Diffusion multimodal large language models rely on confidence to decide when to commit candidate tokens during generation. In multimodal tasks, however, confidence cannot distinguish whether a candidate originates from image evidence or the language prior. We perform paired forward ablation and find that nearly nine out of ten high-confidence commits are insensitive to the image, while degenerate and hallucination samples exhibit significant increases in the entropy of deep-layer attention organization. Based on this diagnosis, we propose CD-APC, a training-free decoding method. CD-APC performs evidence-adjusted scoring within a base-supported pool and uses dual gating based on model acceptability and contrastive concentration to decide whether to commit, together with an inverse-window mechanism that adapts to inter-step difficulty. Across two backbones and five benchmarks, CD-APC consistently improves performance, indicating that stable visual evidence improves model outputs.

papers.title: Exact Collision Gradients for Ellipsoids in Differentiable Simulation
papers.abstract: Differentiable simulation enables gradient-based optimization in learning and control problems involving collisions, but its gradients are least reliable at the moment of impact, when the velocities jump. A fixed-step simulator detects a collision only after the bodies overlap, and some differentiable simulators correct for this with a linear estimate of the time of impact. In this paper, we study impacts between ellipsoids. We show that the gradient error of this estimate grows with the obliqueness of the collision, the curvature at contact, and the time step, and that ignoring spin adds a further error. Subsequently, we find the time of impact with continuous collision detection on the Perram Wertheim contact function and differentiate through the touching condition rather than the search. This gives exact gradients at any step size. We demonstrate our method on an optimal control problem and a system identification problem. In both, exact gradients recover the optimal control and the true parameters, while the linear estimate does not, even when it accounts for spin.

papers.title: Generalized Tate--Nakayama duality for complexes of tori over local function fields
papers.abstract: We define the cohomology set $H^{1}(\mathcal{E}, Z \to T \to U)$ for a complex $Z \to T \to U$ with $T$, $U$ tori over a local function field $F$ and $Z$ a finite subgroup of $T$, where $\mathcal{E}$ is the gerbe from [Dil23]. We follow the method of [Kal26] and prove that the Tate--Nakayama isomorphism [Dil23, Theorem 4.10] for $H^{1}(\mathcal{E}, Z \to T)$ extends to $H^{1}(\mathcal{E}, Z \to T \to U)$, which lets one generalize Kaletha's parametrization [Kal21] of supercuspidal $L$-packets to local function fields.

papers.title: Translation Validation of SystemVerilog-to-SystemC RTL Conversion by Reading the Generated C++
papers.abstract: SystemC models of register-transfer level (RTL) designs are used for virtual platforms, firmware bring-up and simulation without a commercial license, and more of them now come from translators and language models. A wrong model usually compiles, and it usually agrees with the RTL. SystemVerilog evaluates an 8-bit sum in 8 bits while C++ evaluates it in 64, so a translation that forgets one truncation keeps a carry the RTL drops, and only inputs near the top of the range show it. I built svcc, an open-source SystemVerilog-to-SystemC converter, and my first check of its output read the generated C++ with SystemVerilog's rules. That check passed two wrong models. The check that replaced it gives the generated header the meaning C++17 and SystemC give it and turns undefined behavior into proof obligations. It prints what it read as SystemVerilog with every width change explicit, then proves that equivalent to a netlist of the source by induction over registers matched by name. On 50 author-written designs it proves 45 and reports 5 as outside its model. In a mutation experiment it accepted none of the 17 mutants that compiled SystemC showed to be wrong. Of 2,184 modules from 16 open-source code bases, 1,185 conversions match Verilator in random co-simulation and the check proves 600 of them. The same runs found defects in the front end, in svcc and in Verilator.

papers.title: Medical Image Segmentation Is Now Just Another Coding Task
papers.abstract: For decades, every new medical image segmentation task has needed an expert, a dedicated architecture, and a framework such as nnU-Net. This is no longer the case: medical image segmentation is now just another coding task. Given only a task description, labeled data, and a CPU (with no segmentation framework, no pretrained weights, and no human in the loop), four off-the-shelf coding agents built segmenters for 13 tasks across four imaging modalities within hours, an ability that has emerged rather than been built. On the nine 2D tasks, their best programs reach 99% of the Dice of a GPU-trained nnU-Net. Like any code, a segmenter improves by being revised and checked, so we ask how far the same agents can improve their own segmentations and what unlocks further gains. On unseen cases there is no reference, so the agents inspect renderings of their own predictions: this alone lifts the worst tenth of cases by 0.09 Dice and cuts boundary error (HD95) by almost a quarter. Far more is within reach. Told the true Dice of each attempt, the same agents improve in all 14 matched pairs, rescue 85% of failed masks instead of 30%, and surpass the GPU-trained nnU-Net on average, by producing better masks rather than by choosing among them. What unlocks these gains is a quality signal, which neither visual inspection, nor more rounds, nor a quality estimator trained by the agents themselves yet supplies: we call this the quality blind spot. The ability to build and to repair is already present; the next advance will come not from another segmentation model, but from reference-free quality estimation that coding agents can call.

papers.title: Photocatalytic Water Splitting in GeC/ReS$_2$ van der Waals Heterostructures
papers.abstract: Photocatalytic water splitting is considered as one of the most promising approaches for the green hydrogen production. But the rapid recombination of photogenerated electron-hole pairs severely inhibits its photocatalytic efficiency. Construction of van der Waals heterostructures is a good way to suppress this recombination. However, in staggered band heterostructures, the charge transfer could occur either through the type-II or the direct Z-scheme mechanism. Therefore it is very important to identify which mechanism is dominant. In the present work, we systematically study the GeC/ReS$_2$ heterostructure using first-principles density functional theory (DFT). The system exhibits good thermodynamic, dynamic and thermal stability and an indirect band gap of 1.38 eV which greatly enhances the visible-light absorption. We find that the direct Z-scheme mechanism is the dominant interfacial charge transfer by analysing band alignment and Gibbs free energy pathways. The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) can be driven spontaneously in the pH range $4 \le \text{pH} \le 14$ under light irradiation for both type-II and Z-scheme pathways but the energy barrier is much lower for the Z-scheme mechanism. Moreover, the type-II mechanism is not suitable for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), but the Z-scheme mechanism can promote HER well in the entire pH range ($0 \le \text{pH} \le 14$). Remarkably, the strain-free (pristine) condition exhibits a solar-to-hydrogen (STH) efficiency of 41.40\%, well above the 10\% threshold for commercial viability. The STH efficiency is further enhanced to 60.68\% under a tensile strain of +6\%. To summarise, the Z-scheme strain-tunable GeC/ReS$_2$ heterostructure is a promising and efficient photocatalyst for overall water splitting.

papers.title: AeroPoint: Agentic AI for Intent-Driven Point Cloud Inspection in UAV-Edge Systems
papers.abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-based Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) inspection generates dense point clouds that strain onboard computing and wireless bandwidth. Intent-based inspection allows operators to request objects, attributes, and spatial relationships through natural language. Answering these requests requires trans- lating intent into spatial queries and retrieving relevant evidence under UAV processing and communication constraints. This article presents AeroPoint, an agentic AI system combining onboard point cloud processing and knowledge graph construction with Large Language Model (LLM)-based retrieval planning at a ground edge server. The LLM translates inspection questions into structured requests, which the UAV executes to return selected graph evidence for answer generation. We evaluate the prototype in a power line inspection case study using 150 TS40K UAV LiDAR scenes and profile processing costs on NVIDIA Jetson Nano hardware. Retrieval experiments use graphs constructed from dataset-provided ground-truth semantic labels. Experimental results show that transmitted payload decreases from 3700 KB for complete point clouds to 3.1 KB for retrieval responses, while evaluated LLM routers achieve the highest graph retrieval completeness for relational queries.

papers.title: Neural Interoperability Protocols: Specifying Compatibility Before Training
papers.abstract: Neural networks are increasingly developed as reusable components, yet their intermediate representations remain difficult to exchange across independently trained models. Existing approaches can align representations or encourage compatible features, but successful transfer between particular models does not by itself define what future implementations must satisfy to interoperate. We introduce Neural Interoperability Protocols (NIPs), a specification-first framework that treats neural compatibility as a set of public interface obligations rather than a property inferred solely from model-pair performance. A NIP specifies an exchange boundary, the semantics and admissibility conditions of exchanged packets, and the downstream computations that recipients must support, independently of the architectures and training procedures implementing it. We investigate this distinction through controlled retrieval, vision, and continuous-memory experiments involving independently trained models, differing architectures and objectives, and later training cohorts. Matched-competence controls demonstrate that native task success does not ensure interoperability, while shared semantic supervision enables substantial direct transfer in the evaluated settings. Withheld-information experiments show that recipient models can continue computations requiring information unavailable to donors at exchange time. Partial-contract experiments and packet interventions further establish that observed compatibility is conditional on the semantics, packet populations, and recipient continuations being evaluated. Together, these results support public neural interface specifications as a framework for designing prospective component exchange and distinguishing demonstrated interoperability from stronger conformance claims.

papers.title: Equivariant Levi restriction
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group over $\bbC$, $L\subset G$ a Levi subgroup, and $\cL\subset\cG$ their Langlands duals. Macerato \cite{macerato2023leviequivariantrestrictionsphericalperverse} computed the $\cL(\calO)$-equivariant cohomology of the $!$-restriction to $\GrL$ of the regular spherical perverse sheaf on $\GrG$, and identified it with the functions on the partial Kostant--Whittaker reduction $T^*(G/U,\psiL)$, where $\psiL$ is the possibly degenerate Whittaker character of $U$ determined by $L$. We add loop rotation. Our main result is: the $\LO$-equivariant cohomology of the same object is the ring $\Dh(G/U,\psiL)$ of asymptotic $\psiL$-twisted differential operators on $G/U$. For a single $\IC_V$ the answer is the space of intertwiners $\bM_\hbar(\psiL)\to V\otimes\bM_\hbar(\psiL)$ of the universal Verma--Whittaker module. This interpolates between results of Bezrukavnikov--Finkelberg ($L=G$) and Ginzburg--Riche ($L=T$).

papers.title: Provenance Loss and Repair in Multilingual Compaction
papers.abstract: Conversational assistants compact older messages into short notes and evict the originals. When the note's language requires a distinction that English leaves open, such as Spanish adjective gender (agotado vs. agotada), messages that omit or explicitly state that attribute can yield the same note. After eviction, later turns cannot tell them apart: taking the inflected form literally asserts an attribute the user never gave, whereas discounting it as routine grammar discards one the user did give. We propose a training-free repair across writing, pre-eviction verification and reading. The writer marks unstated attributes with paired forms (e.g., agotado/a), a likelihood check before eviction rewrites unsupported single forms into paired ones, and the reader trusts remaining single forms as stated facts. On five Qwen3.5 and Gemma-4 models, eviction cuts recall of stated attributes from 90% to 34% in question answering (QA); our repair raises F1 (which penalizes both errors) on every model, by 9-53 points in QA and 12-40 points in agent handovers.

papers.title: Exteroceptive Sensor Faults in Autonomous Vehicles: A Cross-Modal Taxonomy and Fault Injection Toolkit
papers.abstract: Autonomous vehicles rely on cameras, LiDAR, and radar to perceive their surroundings, yet these exteroceptive sensors can be degraded by hardware aging, environmental interference, miscalibration, embedded software errors, and combinations of these causes, with direct consequences for perception quality and safety. Existing surveys and benchmarks mostly address individual sensors, isolated conditions, or vehicle-level consequences, and no common vocabulary relates fault origins across the three modalities. This paper reviews the literature on exteroceptive sensor faults and proposes a cross-modal, origin-driven taxonomy that organizes them into five categories, namely hardware, environmental, calibration, software, and synergistic faults, mapping each entry to its physical or logical mechanism, observable manifestation, and affected subsystem, and relating the categories to the safety analyses of ISO 26262 and ISO 21448. To make the taxonomy operational, we release an open-source fault injection toolkit with 94 symptom-level routines (41 camera, 27 LiDAR, and 26 radar), four graded severity levels, reproducible burst scheduling, and per-frame labels recording the fault category, affected subsystem, and severity. Examples on the Boreas dataset illustrate how each category alters camera images, LiDAR point clouds, and radar scans. Together, the taxonomy and the toolkit provide a shared reference and a controlled testbed for studying sensor reliability, developing and benchmarking fault detection and diagnosis methods, and building fault-annotated datasets for the safety validation of perception systems. The toolkit is publicly available at https://github.com/davidepossenti/AV-SensorFault-Toolkit.

papers.title: A Piecewise-Linear Activation Function for Implicit Neural Representations
papers.abstract: Coordinate networks with ReLU activations perform poorly on implicit neural representation tasks, and the activations that address this, such as sinusoids and Gabor wavelets, all leave the piecewise-linear function class, so it remains unclear which property of ReLU is at fault. We introduce JaSIN, a family of bounded piecewise-linear activations that interpolates between ReLU and a piecewise-linear sinusoid without any the use of transcendental operation. Our results show that a bounded range improves image reconstruction PSNR on average by 0.06 dB, a single bump 3.29 dB, and centering that bump a further 3.64 dB. The oscillation count improves 6.30 dB more, raising ReLU from 24.0 to 37.3 dB on Kodak images, placing third over eleven activations, within 1.3 dB of the state-of-the-art, though beyond four oscillations the reconstruction collapses. Because an INR is fit on the grid on which it is evaluated, a unit whose pre-activations never reach the support of its activation is certifiably inactive over the entire domain; deleting such units is lossless without fine-tuning, removing up to 84% of parameters at zero loss in performance (dB) and decoding 3.2 times faster. Reference code and demos are available at https://github.com/jeovafarias/jasin.

papers.title: A Proof of the Ovals Conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove that the lowest eigenvalue of the periodic Schrödinger operator $-\partial_s^2+κ^2$ on a closed curve of length $\ell$ is at least $4π^2/\ell^2$. Equality holds precisely for the family of ovals described by Benguria and Loss. The proof uses a new comparison argument for scalar ordinary differential equations.

papers.title: LineEX: Data Extraction from Scientific Line Charts
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce LINEEX that extracts data from scientific line charts. We adapt existing vision transformers and pose detection methods and showcase significant performance gains over existing SOTA baselines. We also propose a new loss function and present its effectiveness against existing loss functions. In addition, we synthetically created the largest line chart dataset comprising 430K images. The code is available at https://github.com/Shiva-sankaran/LineEX.

papers.title: From invasion to replacement: excursions of the Moran model
papers.abstract: An excursion-theoretic description of the continuous-time Moran model with recurrent mutation is developed. Exploiting its birth--death structure, the killed Moran process is characterized through its Green function, resolvent, Laplace transforms of hitting times, and spectral decomposition. A duality between the Moran model and a pure-death process is also established, yielding a spectral representation of its transition probabilities. The characterization of the killed process leads to a boundary-switching excursion representation in which returning excursions correspond to unsuccessful invasions of an allelic type, whilst switching excursions describe population-wide allelic replacement. The resulting regenerative structure provides the exact joint distribution and Laplace transforms for several path statistics, including the number, height and duration of unsuccessful invasions preceding replacement. Using Doob h-transforms, convergence of the rescaled Moran excursion measures and associated point processes, restricted to excursions exceeding a fixed positive height, to their Wright--Fisher counterparts is established. These transformations also show how the law of a Wright--Fisher diffusion killed upon hitting the boundary can be related to that of a Wright--Fisher diffusion with appropriately transformed mutation parameters.

papers.title: Correcting for Differential Nonresponse Using Past Election Data
papers.abstract: In an election survey, the probability of responding can depend on the vote being measured. When supporters of one candidate are less likely to respond, they are underrepresented in the sample and the estimated vote share is biased. Weighting and multilevel regression and poststratification (MRP) adjust for observed covariates but do not eliminate this bias when response rates differ by vote within demographic groups. We ask whether this differential nonresponse can be corrected using the previous election, whose outcome is known. We estimate a two-parameter correction on the log-odds scale against one election's results, apply it unchanged to the next, and compare the corrected estimates with its results. The application is the Cooperative Election Study for the 2020 and 2024 U.S. presidential elections, with the 436 congressional districts as units. Among validated voters in 2020, Republicans appear in the sample at about 0.6 times the odds of Democrats, and in both elections district-level MRP understates the Republican two-party share by 16 to 18 percentage points on average. A correction estimated on 2020 and applied to 2024 gives 95% posterior predictive bands containing the actual result in 98.2% of districts, compared with 91.5% for a correction on the share scale. About two-thirds of the curvature in the 2024 error was already present in 2020, and the transferred correction removes about 69% of it; the remaining third, a level shift of 1.7 points, and a few districts (several with very large 2020-to-2024 swings) are specific to 2024. We also fit a model for variation in differential nonresponse across districts (Little and Gelman, 1998) and find that the design weights account for about 62% of the selection on the log-odds scale. Two variants that apply the correction within poststratification cells, specified in advance, did not improve on the simpler correction.

papers.title: Boundary Representation-Driven Graph Transformer Modeling for Machining Operation Sequencing
papers.abstract: Machining process planning is inherently complex due to the interdependence between part geometry, machining operations, and evolving manufacturable states. Traditional approaches rely heavily on expert knowledge and rule-based systems, limiting scalability and automation. While recent machine learning methods have shown promise, most operate on simplified geometric representations, such as voxels or hand-crafted features, which fail to fully exploit the rich geometric and topological information encoded in Boundary Representation (B-Rep) models. In this work, we propose a graph transformer-based framework for geometry-to-sequence learning that directly predicts machining operation sequences from B-Rep design geometry. The proposed method constructs topology-aware graphs from B-Rep entities, where faces and their adjacencies are encoded as node and edge features capturing both geometric and relational information. A graph neural network encoder learns geometry-aware embeddings, which are then used to condition a dual-decoder transformer that autoregressively generates machining operation sequences. This formulation enables the model to capture both operation-type prediction and process-level ordering constraints directly from design geometry, without requiring intermediate feature extraction or machining-state representations. Experiments on a dataset of 2,991 synthetic machined parts demonstrate strong performance, achieving 95% accuracy for main operation prediction, 64% accuracy for sub-operation prediction, and 93% accuracy for sequence length prediction. Further analysis shows that the model effectively captures precedence relationships and geometry-dependent constraints inherent in machining processes. These results highlight the potential of B-Rep-driven graph learning for scalable and automated machining process planning.

papers.title: Second-order localization and intersecting O6-planes in scale-separated AdS vacua
papers.abstract: We construct explicit periodic second-order localization corrections to scale-separated AdS$_4$ vacua of massive type IIA supergravity on $T^6/(\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2)$. At first order, the corrections from different O6-plane families simply add. The interactions between intersecting families first enter at second order and could obstruct the continuation of the solution. We find explicit solutions for the warp factor, dilaton, full internal metric and required form fields, including the terms generated by these interactions. The metric at second order contains off-diagonal components. With a common regularization of the singular source terms, we verify the full field equations and the conditions required for a solution on a compact space. Using the pure-spinor formalism, we find that the second-order fields satisfy the supersymmetry conditions accessible at the retained orders.

papers.title: Beyond the quasi-steady approximation: Modeling unsteady flows from steady solution families
papers.abstract: Many flow systems have well-established steady-state relations, but applying them quasi-steadily under unsteady forcing neglects memory effects. This study develops a modeling framework extending steady-state relations to unsteady flows by closing dynamic departures from the instantaneous steady state. Integral conservation laws determine the explicit balance structure, while finite-order temporal closures approximate unresolved spatial dynamics responsible for the memory effect. This formulation preserves the prescribed nonlinear steady-state relations as equilibria under constant forcing. Canonical benchmarks in laminar and turbulent channel flows and shallow-water wave propagation demonstrate that the required temporal structure depends on spatial memory and forcing timescale. First-order relaxation captures viscous diffusion, whereas wave propagation and boundary reflections require higher-order models for oscillatory memory. Modal analysis further reveals that the required dynamic resolution depends on the predicted quantity, with wall shear being more sensitive to higher viscous modes than bulk flow rate. Nonlinear extensions with state-dependent steady relations and dynamic coefficients reproduce transient lag, relaxation, and oscillations under slow-to-moderate forcing, including finite-amplitude regimes. However, rapid finite-amplitude waves expose the limits of locally linearized closures in capturing nonlinear phase dynamics. This framework compactly extends quasi-steady approximations while preserving exact steady-state consistency.

papers.title: Collision Rendering: GPU-Accelerated Trajectory Planning on Sparse Voxel Radiance Fields with Risk-Bounded Collision Checking
papers.abstract: Although radiance fields provide detailed scene representations for robotics, they remain underexplored for trajectory planning, without a widely agreed-upon way to translate learned spatial primitives into reliable collision criteria. To bridge this gap, we introduce Collision Rendering, the first trajectory planning framework on sparse voxel radiance fields (SVR), which supports GPU-accelerated, risk-bounded collision checking and a differentiable collision cost. Our key insight is that the structured volumetric density of SVR allows its rendering pipeline to serve as a fast numerical approximator of collision probability. We approximate the robot with collision spheres and place a coinciding spherical camera at each sphere. Under a probabilistic collision model, we derive an upper bound on each sphere's maximum directional collision probability from the camera's rendering pipeline. Evaluating this bound on the GPU yields a modular collision checker that integrates with established sampling-based planners without an auxiliary geometric map or changes to the learned representation. We further compute a collision cost and its gradients from rendered opacities through the same pipeline, extending the framework to trajectory optimization. Experiments demonstrate millisecond collision checking time on a consumer-grade GPU and collision-free trajectories in all queries, outperforming other radiance field-based planners.

papers.title: The Residual Unitary Case for Almost Elusive Groups
papers.abstract: In this short note, we remove the residual unitary family in Hall's classification of almost elusive classical groups and the corresponding conditional family in the quasiprimitive classification. Using theorems of Zsigmondy and Schinzel together with some elementary number theory arguments, we prove that if n > 4 is odd, f > 1 is even, and r is the unique primitive prime divisor of (2^f)^{2n} - 1, then 4nf divides r - 1. For n > 4 prime and any positive integer f, we deduce that a unique primitive prime divisor r of (2^f)^{2n} - 1 satisfies r > 4nf, except when (n, f, r) = (5, 1, 11). We then obtain two conjugacy classes of derangements of the same prime order in a broader family of unitary subspace actions, and a quadratic lower bound for the number of such classes in the corresponding product actions.

papers.title: BRAG: Bayesian Retrieval Augmented Generation
papers.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) ranks memory chunks by semantic similarity to the query. Many methods improve on this by learning from feedback on what was retrieved, but each is a separate heuristic, with no account of when it is the right choice. We introduce BRAG, a generative model of retrieval with use. Each chunk generates the queries it answers from a mixture of von Mises-Fisher components anchored at its original embedding, and each chunk has a latent utility that drifts over time. The model gives the optimal inference, a closed-form filter that stores a few keys and two scalars per chunk and updates them online from the labels of a curator, and it frames retrieval as a control problem. It also shows when existing methods are optimal. Query averaging, Rocchio-style feedback and frequency reranking are special cases with fixed parameters, NUDGE is the case of one key per chunk with no dynamics, and LADER the limit of one key per past query. On two public long-term memory benchmarks, BRAG matches these methods on queries asked before, as expected, because when nothing changes over time the assumptions behind these special cases hold. On harder problems, where a new chunk makes an old one obsolete, BRAG outscores them. They all stay at plain-search level (Recall@5 0.67-0.71), while BRAG retrieves the new chunk 0.80-0.86 of the time. We also ran BRAG on three of NUDGE's seven text benchmarks, and it matches or beats NUDGE on all three. On nine months of a personal agent's memory (20,640 chunks), BRAG raises Recall@5 on held-out queries from 0.75 to 0.98 and Recall@1 from 0.44 to 0.97, with little change on chunks never queried.

papers.title: Universal spectrum of weakly coupled quantum critical Ising chains
papers.abstract: We study the spectrum of arrays of critical transverse field Ising chains perturbed by a weak inter-chain coupling in the scaling limit, using an exact diagonalization algorithm based on Hamiltonian truncation. As the number of chains is made large, we confirm the existence of excitations below the two particle continuum that can be identified with the celebrated Zamalodchikov $E_8$ theory with small corrections. In addition, we find a distinct $ψ$-particle, with mass $M_\mathrmψ$ which is not contained in the $E_8$ theory. Its ratio to the lowest $E_8$ mass ($M_1$) is a universal number, which we have computed numerically to be $M_\mathrmψ/M_1 = 1.819\cdots$ for a one dimensional array of critical chains. We present evidence that this new state fundamentally involves excitations on neighboring chains, explaining why it has no analogue in the single chain problem. Interestingly the $M_\mathrmψ$ mass has a characteristic scaling dependence on detuning from the critical point that is qualitatively distinct from the $E_8$ masses, which can help identify it in spectroscopic experiments on easy-axis magnetic chain materials.

papers.title: Stranded Compute in AI Inference Workloads: Recovering Value Through Demand Aggregation
papers.abstract: AI inference infrastructure is commonly analyzed as an energy business. Under full total cost accounting it is not: in the reference deployment modeled here, capital recovery is 87.3% of fully loaded cost per token and electricity 3.7%. Because capital accrues per unit time irrespective of use, accelerator value is destroyed by non-utilization rather than by consumption. Yet, SLO qualified goodput reaches only 59.6% of nameplate throughput, and the decomposition of the loss chain shows that 25.2 of the 40.4 lost percentage points arise from scheduling idleness and stranded burst reserve. Both are properties of a tenant's demand portfolio rather than of its silicon, and neither is diversifiable by a single tenant acting alone. Modelling reserve and idle capacity as diversifiable risk, pooling demand across eight imperfectly correlated tenants (rho = 0.3) recovers 7.3 pp of goodput, approximately $0.75M per annum per megawatt of IT capacity, or between 2.8x and 4.9x the entire annual interconnection spend of the deployment that produced it. The implication for neutral colocation and interconnection providers is that the switching and interconnection layer aggregating tenant demand functions as an instrument of capital productivity while being priced as transport.

papers.title: Constructing physical mechanisms with artificial intelligence
papers.abstract: Mechanisms recur across the sciences: the equation for heat in a solid also describes molecular diffusion or a Brownian particle. A mechanism is rarely written in one equation; its operation, boundaries, parameters and closures are stated at different steps of a derivation, where methods that read text or fit formulas miss it. We built an equation-native system that reads the equations of all 2.5 million arXiv manuscripts, and show that mechanisms can be compiled from them and constructed by deterministic calculation. A constructor detaches, transfers, unfolds, composes and joins their parts across disciplines; where parts do not fit, the failure is an equation for the missing term. Constructions turn a threshold reactor into a memory that a weak signal writes, an oscillator into a switch through two changes that each fail alone, and a rhythm into the regulator of a chemical amount, each with conditions for an experimental test.

papers.title: Inviscid limit of steady Navier--Stokes equations with Navier friction boundary conditions in a periodic channel
papers.abstract: The vanishing viscosity limit of the steady incompressible Navier--Stokes equations is studied in a periodic channel with Navier friction boundary conditions, where the slip length is assumed to be a nonnegative power of the viscosity. Depending on this power, the problem falls into subcritical, critical, and supercritical regimes. In each regime, the Navier--Stokes solutions are constructed via the Prandtl expansion, and the validity of the expansion is rigorously justified. By the Prandtl--Batchelor theory, the leading Euler solution is a Couette flow, and the interaction between the interior and boundary-layer profiles is precisely characterized. Of particular interest is the critical regime, in which the leading order Prandtl profile solves a nonlinear steady Prandtl equation with a Robin-type boundary condition. The well-posedness of this problem is established using the von Mises transformation and the implicit function theorem, and an implicit Batchelor--Wood formula is derived that determines the coefficients of the leading order Couette flow from the boundary data. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first well-posedness result for the steady Prandtl equation with a Robin-type boundary condition.

papers.title: Anchoring VAE Fine-Tuning to Its Latent Diffusion Prior
papers.abstract: Pretrained latent diffusion models are effective priors for transfer learning, from geometry estimation to physics simulation. Existing approaches fine-tune the diffusion backbone but freeze the encoder of the VAE to preserve the latent distribution. However, a frozen encoder may miss salient details in non-RGB inputs and is limited to three channels. We introduce Diffusion Prior Anchoring (DPA), a regularizer applied during VAE fine-tuning that uses a score-distillation update to steer latents toward the high-density manifold on which the pretrained diffusion model denoises accurately. We validate DPA across three image and video models (FLUX 3, LTX-Video, Wan2.2) and four tasks: monocular depth estimation, MRI reconstruction, wind-flow simulation, and surface normal estimation, where DPA lowers the prediction error by 7.5% relative to the frozen VAE, 4.9% to decoder-only fine-tuning, and 4.0% to unanchored VAE fine-tuning. Its gain grows the further the target data lies from the RGB training distribution, from 3.3% on monocular depth estimation to 7.2% on complex-valued MRI. DPA also applies to modified VAEs, including pruned and multi-channel variants. With a four-channel VAE that encodes depth and surface normals, it lowers depth estimation error by 9.3%.

papers.title: Sharp History-Length Dependence of Mesh-Uniform Exponential Decay Rates for a Boundary-Memory Euler-Bernoulli Beam
papers.abstract: For a boundary-memory Euler--Bernoulli beam with polynomial relaxation, we quantify the loss of exponential stability as the retained history length $S$ grows. The continuous and conforming Hermite--$\mathbb P_1$ generators have zero-frequency resolvent norms bounded above and below by constant multiples of $S$. The bounds are uniform in the beam mesh and in every history mesh of step at most a fixed $h_0$. Their semigroup norms retain a plateau of duration proportional to $S$. Under positive distributed and boundary damping, matching exponential estimates hold with the optimal time scale $1+S$, uniformly in the meshes. Optimality refers to the semigroup norm on the augmented state space, which includes the history. Without distributed damping, the same time scale holds for the continuous truncated generator under a boundary condition on $δ^{(3)}$. We also prove strong convergence of the finite-history semigroups to the full-history semigroup, uniformly on compact time intervals, under restriction and zero extension of histories. Remote-history packets give residuals of order $S^{-1}$ for the truncated generator and of order $S^{-1}+h$ after discretization, improved to $S^{-1}$ at zero frequency. Numerical tests confirm the residual orders.

papers.title: The Matrix in Pieces: Complete BFSS Scattering at Finite Rank
papers.abstract: As two matrix blocks separate in Banks-Fischler-Shenker-Susskind matrix quantum mechanics, the modes connecting them develop a growing excitation gap. Supersymmetry cancels their leading vacuum energy, so blocks in internal bound states can scatter as composite particles. We prove that these particle channels are asymptotically complete for the physical relative Hamiltonian at each fixed finite rank $N\ge 2$. Because a block can itself break up as its center moves away from the others, the proof must control motion on both scales. Inverse powers of the matrix radius control derivatives along internal flat directions, while the growing gap suppresses excitations between blocks. Propagation estimates then allow us to resolve successive breakups by induction on the block rank. The incoming and outgoing wave operators each have range equal to the absolutely continuous subspace, and the singular-continuous subspace vanishes. The scattering operator is thus unitary when each constituent can occupy any of its internal bound states. For a normalized incoming state of zero-energy constituents, the outgoing probability missing from the zero-energy channels equals the inclusive probability of producing at least one constituent with positive internal energy.

papers.title: MADJEPA: Enhanced Multi-Stage Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for Medical Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract: Anomaly detection in medical images is a complex task, requiring the development of a robust model using only healthy patient data. Without access to labeled data, modern approaches typically employ self-supervised learning to obtain a model of normality. Since world models promise to build strong internal representations of their environment, we consider them as suitable candidates for the medical anomaly detection environment, namely medical investigations of healthy patients. To this end, we propose MADJEPA, a medical anomaly detector based on an enhanced multi-stage joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA). We design a multi-stage training pipeline to produce a robust detector: (1) image-based JEPA (I-JEPA) training aims to learn a strong representation of normal training data; (2) target encoder distillation aims to modulate over-generalization of I-JEPA representations to abnormal data; (3) pseudo-anomaly classification aims to calibrate anomaly predictions by learning a tight boundary around the normal data manifold. To demonstrate our design, we carry out comprehensive experiments on six datasets covering various medical image domains (e.g. MRI, OCT, X-ray, histopathology), comparing our MADJEPA with numerous state-of-the-art methods. The results show that our carefully designed world model, MADJEPA, attains competitive results, ranking first on three datasets. Our ablation studies further confirm the utility of each training stage, indicating that I-JEPA alone is not sufficient to obtain competitive results in medical anomaly detection. We publicly release our code at https://github.com/Sabina085/madjepa.

papers.title: On the High Eccentricity Orbit of 51 Eri b and Constraints on Interactions with a Second Companion
papers.abstract: The eccentricity of an exoplanet's orbit is a key observational quantity that can be used to infer its dynamical past and predict its future orbital evolution. Planets are expected to emerge from their protoplanetary cradles with roughly circular eccentricities, and non-circular eccentricites to arise from subsequent dynamical processing in the absence of the gas disk. We present an updated orbit for 51 Eridani b based on 5 years of 0.2 mas precision optical interferometry from VLTI/GRAVITY(+). This planet is young (${\sim}20\,\mathrm{Myr}$ old), temperate ($T_{\rm eff}\sim650\,\mathrm{K}$), and on a wide orbit ($a{=}9.36\,\mathrm{au}$) with an uncertain mass ($M_{\rm b}\leq12\,M_{\rm J}$). We measured the planet's motion to an exceptionally high precision, confirming that its orbit is very eccentric ($e_b=0.574\pm0.003$). We observe residuals to the absolute astrometry of the host star based on a single planet orbit that could be attributable to reflex motion from a third body in the system. We construct a two companion orbit model that could explain the apparent reflex motion of 51 Eri A: this model predicts that the putative second companion has $M_c\in[1.0, 2900]_{95\%}\,M_{\rm Jup}$ and $a_c\in[0.3, 3.1]_{95\%}\,\mathrm{au}$. In this framework, a dynamical interaction between b and ``c" could have kicked the exterior, lower mass b out onto its present, eccentric orbit. If this signal is astrophysical, and not due to a systematic error, this candidate should be confirmable with Gaia DR4 epoch astrometry in the near future.

papers.title: Observable Spectral Framework for Noisy Amplitude Amplification: Stopping Stability and Correction
papers.abstract: Stopping rules for noisy amplitude amplification often rely on channel-specific success-probability formulas, limiting their transfer across noise mechanisms. We develop an observable spectral framework for stationary noisy standard amplitude amplification with a known ideal success fraction, under explicit leading-mode, spectral-separation, and residual-control conditions. Within this class, the first amplification lobe has a damped-oscillatory leading component and a bounded non-leading contribution. We derive how frequency shift, damping, and observable phase offset displace the leading peak, and establish sampled-gap criteria for retaining the ideal integer stopping depth, certifying recalibration, or selecting a robust candidate window. In single-target Grover search, frequency and damping errors have stopping-coordinate sensitivities proportional to the search-space size, whereas phase offsets scale with its square root; residual modes can independently reverse the ordering of neighbouring depths. Analytical constructions, circuit simulations, finite-shot inference, and calibration-derived device-like trajectories examine these predictions and their operational limits. For a 64-element search, an a posteriori sampled-set check selects depth five over six, with success probability increasing from 0.595 to 0.626. The resulting theory links observable spectral dynamics to conditional integer stopping guarantees without requiring a separate microscopic channel solution.

papers.title: An isolated complex Hadamard matrix with nonzero defect
papers.abstract: The defect of a complex Hadamard matrix is the real dimension of the solution space obtained by linearizing the row orthogonality equations in the phases of the entries, with the first row and column fixed. It is known that defect zero implies isolation up to Hadamard equivalence. The converse, whether every isolated complex Hadamard matrix has defect zero, was open and is the square-matrix case of a conjecture of Banica, Ozteke and Pittau. We answer this question in the negative. We exhibit a Butson-type Hadamard matrix of order 13 with entries among the sixth roots of unity and show that it is isolated and has defect one. We prove isolation by showing that no nonzero solution of the linearized equations satisfies the second order condition obtained by the second author for directions of convergence of sequences of Hadamard matrices. In the language of commuting squares of matrix algebras, the example shows that an isolated commuting square can fail the span condition introduced by the second author as a sufficient condition for isolation.

papers.title: Grid-Forming AI Data Centers: Coordinated Grid Support Control from IT Loads and Energy Storage
papers.abstract: To exploit the grid-support capability of AI data centers (AIDCs), this paper proposes a grid-forming (GFM) control scheme which coordinates the IT loads and energy storage (ES) in the AIDC. First, the framework of a grid-connected AIDC is presented, with the multi-stage power conversion from the grid to the IT loads presented. A dual GFM scheme is then proposed for the back-to-back converters to provide grid support through coordinated power adjustments from IT loads and ES. In addition, an aggregated power response model is established to characterize the IT-load flexibility considering multiple IT servers executing diverse tasks. Time-domain simulations of a 100 MW grid-connected AIDC demonstrate that the proposed control scheme can effectively support the grid.

papers.title: Imaging the two-sided black hole interior with four-point correlators
papers.abstract: We propose a boundary four-point function smeared with wavepackets, which probes local physics behind the horizon of a two-sided AdS black hole. At high frequencies, boundary wavepackets aimed at an interior bulk point travel along geodesics and scatter locally about the bulk point, factorizing the correlator into a flat-space like scattering amplitude. To obtain this configuration, we utilize a non-trivial time ordering of operators, and also use one state-dependent operator insertion moved halfway across the thermal circle. An interesting property of this observable is that it also probes features of nontrivial states: null shocks and matter shells behind the horizon show up as jumps in the observed signal as the bulk point crosses them, thereby imaging the black hole interior.

papers.title: Ramanujan Challenge Results: AI-Assisted Evaluation Pipeline for Multi-Format Proofs
papers.abstract: As AI's mathematical capabilities rapidly improve, meaningful benchmarks are shifting from university-level problems and math olympiads to research-level mathematics. The Ramanujan Challenge is a benchmark comprised of research-level problems in number theory, including unpublished results and open conjectures. It presented concrete formulas for mathematical constants whose correctness can be checked numerically, while their proofs may require non-obvious mathematics. Here, we analyze the Challenge submissions, measuring the relative success of different AI models, Computer Algebra Systems (CAS), and formal tools. We find correct submissions that are conceptually distinct from the official solutions, and a proof of one of the published open conjectures. Evaluating the submissions exposed a second challenge: judging complex proofs reliably at scale. We introduce an AI-assisted evaluation pipeline for natural language proofs, CAS code, and Lean formalizations that assesses semantic and logical correctness. Compared with the conventional one-shot LLM judgment, our pipeline reduces false-positive verdicts on natural language proofs from 23% to 6% and improves judgment accuracy on supporting code from 46% to 58%. This approach provides a methodology for evaluating research-level mathematics at scale, with potential applications across mathematics and AI for science.

papers.title: On the Impact of Alternative Settlement Rules for State-of-Charge-Limited Resources in Electricity Markets
papers.abstract: Standard two-settlement markets compute a participant's total profit as the sum of its day-ahead (DA) profit and its incremental real-time (RT) profit. This rule was designed for conventional generators, which can always deliver their DA schedules in RT because their capacity is the same in both markets. Energy storage resources, in contrast, are limited by their state of charge (SOC), so their ability to honor a DA award depends on the SOC available at the time of RT dispatch. When this SOC is insufficient, the RT market may impose a buy-back or sell-back that can lead to a monetary loss. This paper formalizes this asymmetry between SOC-unlimited and SOC-limited resources and assesses three alternative settlement rules: a zero-profit floor; a max rule, which pays storage the maximum of its RT-only profit and its standard DA plus incremental RT profit; and a variant of the max rule applied only when the standard profit is negative. Through our analysis and a case study based on a realistic version of the California system, we identify when storage is most exposed to losses, assess how the alternative rules let storage deviate from DA awards to provide flexibility, and quantify their impact on revenue adequacy.

papers.title: Tiered Cache Blocking and In-Kernel Task Dispatch for Long-Context Prefill Attention on CPU
papers.abstract: Agentic AI drives significant productivity gains across diverse domains, but concurrent long-context prefills from multiple agents can saturate GPU compute resources. Although CPUs offer a viable alternative, existing CPU attention kernels fall short in adapting to multi-tier cache hierarchies and lack effective thread scheduling. To address this, we introduce TACPU, a high-performance attention kernel featuring tiered cache blocking and an in-kernel task dispatching mechanism designed for causal full-sequence prefilling. TACPU achieves up to a 2.01x speedup over PyTorch SDPA, FlexAttention, and SGLang attention kernels. Integrated into SGLang, it reduces Time to First Token (TTFT) of Llama-3.1-8B by up to 1.74x while preserving model accuracy.

papers.title: Ellipsoid Separation in Data-Dependent Time via Infimal Displacement Vectors
papers.abstract: The infimal displacement vector of the nonexpansive operator underlying the primal-dual hybrid gradient algorithm (PDHG) is known to encode useful information for infeasible optimization problems. In particular, for the ellipsoid separation problem (ESP), where the goal is to find a separating hyperplane between two collections of ellipsoids, the infimal displacement vector corresponding to an infeasible second-order cone program (SOCP) encodes a separating hyperplane. We show FISTA computes a sequence of approximations to the dual component of the infimal displacement vector and establish that a solution to the ESP can be obtained in $\mathcal{O}(δ_{\mathcal{A}}^{-2})$ iterations. We then show how to improve the bound to $\mathcal{O}(δ_{\mathcal{A}}^{-1})$. Here $δ_{\mathcal{A}}$ denotes the distance between the convex hulls of the two ellipsoid collections.

papers.title: Beyond Static Leaderboards: Capability-Focused Evaluation with Structural Diversity for Time Series Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Static public benchmarks for time series foundation models (TSFMs) typically have fixed and narrow test distributions. Their repeated reuse encourages benchmark-specific tuning, making reported performance reflect adaptation to the fixed test set rather than genuine forecasting generalization. In addition, a single aggregate score cannot fully characterize model capabilities across distinct temporal structures and input relationships. We propose CaFE (Capability-Focused Evaluation), a refreshable evaluation extension grounded in original benchmark data that enriches static benchmarks with structural diversity and enriches single-score black-box evaluation with multi-dimensional, capability-oriented assessment. CaFE first profiles the original benchmark and defines eight Structural Features (SFs) that characterize its temporal structure. For each SF, it resamples the original data according to its structural support, removes edge-of-distribution samples, and augments the retained samples by varying the SF's salience, producing samples with different structural profiles. After filtering out out-of-distribution samples while preserving diversity, CaFE yields a refreshed evaluation set. TSFMs are then evaluated on this set using both conventional forecast-error metrics and our proposed intervention-response metrics, giving each model a per-feature capability profile alongside endpoint accuracy. Experiments on GIFT-Eval and FEV-Mini20 show that CaFE yields stable evaluation results and reveals per-feature strengths and weaknesses that a single aggregate score hides. Moreover, on genuine data filtered by structural condition, models selected by CaFE outperform those chosen by the aggregate leaderboard. CaFE therefore makes model selection conditional on the structural response of interest.

papers.title: When Weak Reports Matter: Staged Anchored Fusion for Cooperative UAV Sensing
papers.abstract: An echo rejected locally may still help other receivers confirm a target. Staged anchored recovery (SAR) retains confirmations based on strong reports, then uses unused strong reports to retrieve compatible weak evidence. This retrieval preserves every remaining candidate containing a strong report once the initial associations are fixed. We derive sharp bounds on corroborating support when receivers have different evidence probabilities and arbitrary dependence, constructing a joint distribution that attains every value between the bounds. For advance source selection with nonnegative additive costs, any feasible worst-case true/false support constraints can be met optimally by querying no weak-report source or just one. Simulations of unmanned aerial vehicle sensing show additional recoveries over strict consensus, sometimes accompanied by more unmatched outputs. In further tests, recovered positions often lack full velocity estimates, shared reflections create false confirmations, and query overhead can exceed upload savings.

papers.title: GS-Pool: Object-Level Change Detection in 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.abstract: Many physical spaces require photographic monitoring of changes to their structure over time. When each visit is reconstructed with 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), a direct comparison of the two reconstructions cannot answer this because training is stochastic and two reconstructions of an unchanged space never coincide. To address this, we propose GS-Pool, which takes two independently reconstructed Gaussian scans of the same space and returns the changed objects in each, together with their change masks. Our method begins by extracting SAM2 masks from the photographs of each visit. These are then lifted onto the Gaussians that render them and merged into an object pool, a collection of 3D objects, so every decision is taken once per object in 3D. We introduce a novel photographic carrier approach, which co-opts the existing 3DGS mechanism. It does so by applying the photographs of the other visit and back-propagating them to the Gaussians that rendered each pixel. We combine this with GS-Diff's geometry and colour terms and our distilled DINOv3 features. This evidence is compared with objects identified as unchanged in both visits to set a change threshold for each scene. On the PASLCD benchmark, GS-Pool achieves mIoU/F1 scores of 0.75/0.85 against 0.64/0.76 for GS-Diff, the strongest offline method for detecting change in 3DGS. Finally, we return each changed object as a set of Gaussians, which can be inspected in 3D.

papers.title: Lattice in Line: Optimized DMRG ordering for complex lattice geometries
papers.abstract: The density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) is a one-dimensional tensor-network technique, but it is not limited to one-dimensional systems: it can be applied to periodic 2D and 3D clusters and molecules, provided their sites are first enumerated along a line; a step one may call ``lattice compilation''. This paper discusses three proxy loss functions for finding this optimal enumeration: the graph bandwidth $B$ (maximum interaction range), the cutwidth $C$ (maximum number of bonds crossing a cut), and the average interaction range $R$. Constructing the Hamiltonian MPO (matrix-product operator) for a large set of clusters that are of interest in frustrated magnetism, I find that $C$ determines the peak SU(2) Heisenberg MPO bond dimension and $R$ the average one. Targeting $(C,R)$ lexicographically yields the best energies. Targeting $B$ indirectly reduces $C$, but not as efficiently as targeting $C$ directly. Otherwise, the value of $B$ itself is largely irrelevant in the sense that good DMRG energies can have large $B$.
